heuristics.rule: Master's degree graduates (any program length) receive a 3-year PGWP effective February 15, 2024
heuristics.condition: When an international student completes a master's degree at an eligible Canadian DLI on or after February 15, 2024
heuristics.action: Apply for a 3-year PGWP regardless of whether the master's program was 1 year or 2 years in length
heuristics.because: IRCC changed the PGWP duration rule for master's degrees effective February 15, 2024 — previously a 1-year master's yielded only a 1-year PGWP
heuristics.regulatory_basis: IRCC PGWP program page; IRCC press release February 15, 2024

heuristics.rule: Target direct-hire Fortune 100 tech employers over IT consulting/outsourcing firms for H-1B sponsorship
heuristics.condition: When an international student is evaluating which employers to target for H-1B sponsorship
heuristics.action: Prioritize direct-hire tech and finance companies (avg 97.4% approval, 0.9% denial, 6.1% RFE rate) over IT consulting/outsourcing firms (avg 78.2% approval, 12.7% denial, 38.8% RFE rate)
heuristics.because: USCIS FY2025 data shows a 19.2 percentage point gap in approval rates and a 32.7 percentage point gap in RFE rates between these employer categories
heuristics.regulatory_basis: USCIS H-1B Employer Data Hub FY2025; H1B Data Hub analysis of USCIS public disclosure data

heuristics.rule: PhD graduates receive a 3-year PGWP regardless of program length effective February 15, 2024
heuristics.condition: When an international student completes a doctoral (PhD) degree at an eligible Canadian DLI on or after February 15, 2024
heuristics.action: Apply for a 3-year PGWP
heuristics.because: IRCC updated the PGWP duration rule for doctoral degrees effective February 15, 2024
heuristics.regulatory_basis: IRCC PGWP program page; IRCC press release February 15, 2024

heuristics.rule: Employer must register H-1B candidate by March 1–18 for October 1 start date
heuristics.condition: When an employer intends to sponsor a new H-1B worker subject to the annual cap
heuristics.action: Secure offer and complete employer registration during the March 1–18 USCIS registration window; offer and processing must be in place by February at the latest
heuristics.because: USCIS H-1B lottery registration window is fixed at March 1–18 each year; selected registrants then file full petition for October 1 start date
heuristics.regulatory_basis: USCIS H-1B Annual Cap and Lottery structure; USCIS H-1B Employer Data Hub FY2025

heuristics.rule: Programs of 8 months to under 2 years yield a PGWP equal to the length of the program
heuristics.condition: When an international student completes a program of 8 months to under 2 years (other than a master's or PhD)
heuristics.action: Expect a PGWP matching the program's duration, not a fixed 3-year term
heuristics.because: IRCC duration rules post-February 15, 2024 only grant automatic 3-year PGWPs to master's, PhD, and programs of 2 years or longer
heuristics.regulatory_basis: IRCC PGWP program page; IRCC press release February 15, 2024

heuristics.rule: Employer must pay whichever is higher: prevailing wage or actual wage
heuristics.condition: When an employer files an H-1B petition for any worker
heuristics.action: Employer must certify and pay either (1) the prevailing wage — average wage paid to similarly employed workers in the same occupation and geographic area — or (2) the actual wage paid to other workers with similar skills/qualifications, whichever is higher
heuristics.because: DOL prevailing wage requirement creates a legal floor; paying below this floor constitutes a violation of the Labor Condition Application (LCA) terms
heuristics.regulatory_basis: DOL OFLC Performance Data; DOL prevailing wage requirements for H-1B

heuristics.rule: Programs of 2 years or longer yield a 3-year PGWP
heuristics.condition: When an international student completes a program of 2 years or longer (other than master's or PhD)
heuristics.action: Apply for a 3-year PGWP
heuristics.because: The 3-year PGWP for programs 2 years or longer was unchanged by the February 15, 2024 updates
heuristics.regulatory_basis: IRCC PGWP program page; IRCC press release February 15, 2024

heuristics.rule: Avoid IT staffing firms if H-1B approval certainty is a priority
heuristics.condition: When evaluating IT staffing firms as potential H-1B sponsors
heuristics.action: Treat IT staffing firm sponsorship as high-risk: approval rates of approximately 60–75%, denial rates approaching 20%, and RFE rates of 35%+
heuristics.because: USCIS FY2025 data identifies IT staffing firms as the lowest-performing employer category for H-1B approvals
heuristics.regulatory_basis: H1B Data Hub analysis of USCIS FY2025 public disclosure data

heuristics.rule: Bachelor's degree graduates must have studied in an eligible field of study to receive a PGWP effective November 1, 2024
heuristics.condition: When an international student graduates from a bachelor's degree program starting on or after November 1, 2024
heuristics.action: Verify that the field of study is on the IRCC-approved eligible fields list before applying for PGWP
heuristics.because: IRCC implemented field of study requirements for bachelor's level graduates effective November 1, 2024; 178 fields were removed from eligibility
heuristics.regulatory_basis: IRCC field of study requirements for PGWP; IRCC notice November 1, 2024

heuristics.rule: Verify employer H-1B history using USCIS Employer Data Hub before accepting offer
heuristics.condition: When an international student is evaluating a job offer from a potential H-1B sponsor
heuristics.action: Search the employer on USCIS H-1B Employer Data Hub (uscis.gov/tools/reports-and-studies/h-1b-employer-data-hub) to see petition counts and approval history; also check DOL OFLC Disclosure Data for prevailing wages for the specific occupation and location
heuristics.because: Approval rates vary dramatically by employer; an uninformed acceptance of an offer from a low-approval-rate sponsor creates material immigration risk
heuristics.regulatory_basis: USCIS H-1B Employer Data Hub; DOL OFLC Performance Data (dol.gov/agencies/eta/foreign-labor/performance)

heuristics.rule: Master's and PhD graduates are exempt from the field of study requirement
heuristics.condition: When an international student holds a master's or PhD degree from an eligible Canadian DLI
heuristics.action: Apply for the 3-year PGWP without regard to field of study
heuristics.because: IRCC explicitly exempts master's and PhD graduates from the field of study requirement introduced November 1, 2024
heuristics.regulatory_basis: IRCC field of study requirements for PGWP

heuristics.rule: Cap-exempt employers are not subject to the 85,000 annual H-1B cap
heuristics.condition: When an international student is considering employment at a university, affiliated research institution, government research organization, or nonprofit research organization
heuristics.action: Recognize that these employers can file H-1B petitions at any time of year without lottery participation and without being subject to the 85,000 annual cap
heuristics.because: USCIS designates universities, affiliated research institutions, government research organizations, and nonprofit research organizations as cap-exempt
heuristics.regulatory_basis: USCIS H-1B Annual Cap and Lottery structure; USCIS H-1B Employer Data Hub FY2025

heuristics.rule: PGWP applicants who apply before their study permit expires may work under maintained status while the application is pending
heuristics.condition: When a PGWP application is pending and the graduate applied before their study permit expired
heuristics.action: The graduate may work under the maintained status provision during the approximately 8-month processing period
heuristics.because: IRCC's maintained status provision preserves work authorization during a pending PGWP application provided the application was filed before study permit expiry

heuristics.rule: Employer must be E-Verify enrolled to sponsor STEM OPT
heuristics.condition: When an employer is evaluating sponsoring a student on STEM OPT extension
heuristics.action: Confirm employer is enrolled in E-Verify as a separate requirement from H-1B sponsorship capability
heuristics.because: E-Verify enrollment is a distinct and mandatory requirement for STEM OPT sponsorship, separate from H-1B sponsorship eligibility
heuristics.regulatory_basis: USCIS H-1B Employer Data Hub guidance; STEM OPT E-Verify requirement

heuristics.rule: LMIA-backed job offer points have been removed from the Express Entry CRS effective Spring 2025
heuristics.condition: When an Express Entry candidate holds an LMIA-backed job offer after Spring 2025
heuristics.action: Do not count on receiving 50 or 200 additional CRS points for that job offer
heuristics.because: Minister Marc Miller announced December 18, 2024 that arranged employment points via LMIA route were removed from the CRS to address fraud and increase fairness
heuristics.regulatory_basis: Minister Marc Miller announcement December 18, 2024; IRCC Express Entry updates

heuristics.rule: Work in NOC TEER 4 or 5 does not count toward CEC eligibility even if full-time and legally authorized
heuristics.condition: When a PGWP holder is employed in a NOC TEER 4 or TEER 5 occupation (e.g., retail sales clerk, food service worker)
heuristics.action: Recognize that this employment does not accumulate CEC-eligible Canadian work experience regardless of hours or duration
heuristics.because: CEC eligibility requires work in NOC TEER 0, 1, 2, or 3; TEER 4 and TEER 5 are explicitly excluded from CEC qualifying experience
heuristics.regulatory_basis: IRCC CEC requirements; NOC TEER system

heuristics.rule: Students in bachelor's programs affected by the November 1, 2024 field of study removal may have transitional protection if they started before that date
heuristics.condition: When a bachelor's degree student began a program in a field removed from PGWP eligibility before November 1, 2024
heuristics.action: Assess eligibility for transitional protection before assuming PGWP ineligibility
heuristics.because: IRCC indicated that students in affected programs who started before November 1, 2024 may have transitional protection
heuristics.regulatory_basis: IRCC field of study requirements for PGWP

heuristics.rule: If you are working in Retail or Food Services on a PGWP, your PR clock has not started
heuristics.condition: When a PGWP holder is employed in TEER 4/5 occupations (retail, food services) and believes they are accumulating PR-qualifying experience...
heuristics.action: ...recognize that CEC requires TEER 0-3 experience, and begin actively transitioning to a TEER 0-3 role before the PGWP expires
heuristics.because: TEER 4/5 employment is legally valid on an open work permit but does not count toward Canadian Experience Class — you can work for years and still be ineligible for the most common PR pathway

heuristics.rule: When a small company says 'we don't sponsor,' treat it as a cost objection, not a policy rejection
heuristics.condition: When a company with fewer than 200 employees declines to sponsor H-1B
heuristics.action: Probe whether the barrier is legal cost/compliance uncertainty rather than opposition to hiring internationally, and explore whether a sponsorship assistance arrangement is negotiable
heuristics.because: The real blocker for small companies is $5,000–$15,000 in filing and attorney fees per petition, not ideological opposition — removing the cost barrier can change the outcome

heuristics.rule: French CLB 7 is worth more CRS points than 2-3 years of additional Canadian work experience for most PGWP holders
heuristics.condition: When a PGWP holder is stuck below the general Express Entry cut-off (480-520) and does not speak French...
heuristics.action: ...calculate whether investing in French language training to reach CLB 7 would yield more points faster than waiting for work experience points to accumulate
heuristics.because: French CLB 7+ adds ~25 points and unlocks French-language proficiency draws with cut-offs 80-120 points lower than general draws, which is equivalent to several years of additional Canadian work experience in CRS terms

heuristics.rule: Target cap-exempt employers first if you want to eliminate lottery risk entirely
heuristics.condition: When an international graduate is evaluating first post-OPT employer options and wants to avoid the 35% annual H-1B lottery odds
heuristics.action: Prioritize roles at universities, non-profit research organizations, or government research labs (NIH, NASA, national labs) which are fully exempt from the 85,000 annual cap
heuristics.because: Cap-exempt H-1B filings are approved without entering the lottery, eliminating a structural risk that blocks 65% of new applicants annually

heuristics.rule: When an employer says 'we don't sponsor,' proactively clarify you hold an open work permit before accepting the rejection
heuristics.condition: When a PGWP holder encounters an employer who declines to proceed citing sponsorship or immigration compliance concerns...
heuristics.action: ...state explicitly: 'I hold an open work permit — no employer action, cost, or paperwork is required to hire me'
heuristics.because: 22% of Canadian employers surveyed misunderstood PGWP rules and believed they needed to sponsor; most objections are based on misinformation, not actual policy

heuristics.rule: Once your first H-1B is approved, treat employer lock-in as solved — not ongoing
heuristics.condition: When an H-1B worker is evaluating whether to stay at a first employer out of immigration fear
heuristics.action: Recognize that H-1B portability under AC21 allows immediate employer transfer upon new petition filing, without re-entering the cap or waiting for new approval
heuristics.because: The lock-in risk is concentrated at the first-petition stage; after approval the worker can change jobs administratively without lottery re-entry

heuristics.rule: Master's degree holders should prioritize CEC or OINP Masters Graduate stream first, not FSW
heuristics.condition: When a Canadian master's graduate with a PGWP is evaluating PR pathways...
heuristics.action: ...default toward CEC (if TEER 0-3 employment is secured) or OINP Masters Graduate stream (if not yet in skilled employment), rather than Federal Skilled Worker
heuristics.because: CEC was the PR pathway for ~55% of successful PGWP PR conversions; OINP Masters Graduate stream uniquely does not require skilled work experience, providing a workaround for graduates without TEER 0-3 roles

heuristics.rule: Use publicly available LCA wage data to benchmark H-1B offers before accepting
heuristics.condition: When evaluating a compensation offer tied to an H-1B sponsorship
heuristics.action: Cross-reference the offered salary against DOL H-1B LCA disclosure data at H1BData.info for the specific role level and metro area
heuristics.because: H-1B wage data is public by law; a below-market offer combined with sponsorship dependency is a structural disadvantage that can be identified and negotiated before signing

heuristics.rule: Plan financially assuming a 10-25% wage discount versus domestic peers for the first 2-3 years
heuristics.condition: When an international student is budgeting for post-graduation life in Canada...
heuristics.action: ...model your first salary at 10-25% below what a comparable domestic graduate earns, and do not base housing or debt repayment plans on domestic graduate salary benchmarks
heuristics.because: Statistics Canada data shows a persistent initial wage gap that is real even if temporary — over-leveraging on cost-of-living assumptions based on domestic salary expectations creates financial risk

heuristics.rule: If long-term US residency is the goal, model the full immigration timeline — not just the H-1B step
heuristics.condition: When a job seeker from India or China is planning a US-only career strategy
heuristics.action: Factor in 50+ year green card backlogs for India/China against 18–30 month Canadian PR timelines for the same profile, and treat Canada as a legitimate parallel path rather than fallback
heuristics.because: The H-1B is only one step; the green card backlog can mean permanent temporary status for decades, which changes the risk calculus of a US-only strategy fundamentally

heuristics.rule: If you cannot secure TEER 0-3 employment in Ontario, explore smaller provinces before the PGWP expires
heuristics.condition: When a PGWP holder in a major urban centre is struggling to secure skilled employment and PR-eligible experience...
heuristics.action: ...evaluate Saskatchewan, Manitoba, or Nova Scotia where PNP streams are specifically designed for international graduates of provincial institutions and CRS cut-offs are lower
heuristics.because: Smaller provinces have less competition, dedicated PNP streams for international graduates, and lower CRS nomination thresholds — the PR path may be faster even if salaries are lower

heuristics.rule: If your Canadian master's program is 2+ years, you get a 3-year PGWP; if it's 1 year, you get a 1-year PGWP — the program length decision is effectively an immigration decision.
heuristics.condition: When an international student is selecting between a 1-year and 2-year Canadian master's program...
heuristics.action: ...treat the extra year of study as purchasing 2 additional years of open work authorization, not just an academic upgrade
heuristics.because: A 3-year PGWP creates enough runway to accumulate 1 year of skilled work experience, apply for CEC, and receive PR before the permit expires — a 1-year PGWP does not

heuristics.rule: With a 3-year PGWP, you have 18-24 months to land a TEER 0/1/2/3 role and accumulate 12 months before needing to file for CEC
heuristics.condition: When you are a PGWP holder beginning your post-graduation job search in Canada
heuristics.action: Prioritize getting into any qualifying TEER 0/1/2/3 role quickly over finding the ideal role, treating Phase 1 as timeline management not career optimization
heuristics.because: Every month spent unemployed or in TEER 4/5 work compresses or eliminates the CEC window, forcing reliance on renewal, alternative streams, or leaving Canada

heuristics.rule: Never ask for a job or referral in the first cold message
heuristics.condition: When sending an initial cold email or LinkedIn message to someone you have no prior relationship with...
heuristics.action: ...ask only for a 20-minute conversation on a specific topic, never mention openings or referrals
heuristics.because: Asking for a job in the first message destroys the relationship before it starts — the social capital required for a referral hasn't been built yet

heuristics.rule: Target hiring managers who have been in their role less than 2 years
heuristics.condition: When doing cold outreach to hiring managers at target companies...
heuristics.action: ...prioritize managers with tenure under 2 years over longer-tenured ones
heuristics.because: Newer managers are more receptive to outreach, likely still building their teams and more open to non-traditional candidate pipelines

heuristics.rule: If a sponsor asks you to pay any H-1B filing fees, stop the process immediately regardless of how legitimate they otherwise appear
heuristics.condition: When any employer or staffing firm requests payment for I-129 petition fees, ACWIA training fees, premium processing, or attorney fees...
heuristics.action: ...treat it as a definitive scam signal and exit the arrangement
heuristics.because: Charging workers for H-1B fees is explicitly illegal under INA § 212(n), so any company doing this is already in violation of federal law before you've even started

heuristics.rule: Most offers are won at network activation and outreach steps, not at application submission
heuristics.condition: When deciding how to allocate job search time and energy...
heuristics.action: ...spend 50%+ of time on cold outreach, referral requests, and networking with strangers rather than submitting applications
heuristics.because: ATS systems filter out 75-90% of applicants before human review; a referral guarantees human eyes on your resume, which is the actual bottleneck

heuristics.rule: Filter companies for sponsorship willingness before investing in applications or relationships
heuristics.condition: When you are an international student beginning your job search...
heuristics.action: ...use USCIS H-1B disclosure data, LinkedIn/Handshake filters, and alumni networks to build a sponsor-confirmed target list before sending a single application
heuristics.because: Applying broadly to unvetted companies wastes effort and risks discovering sponsorship ineligibility after significant emotional and time investment

heuristics.rule: If you are 12–18 months from graduation, your primary job search goal is securing an internship at your target employer, not a full-time job
heuristics.condition: When an international student is planning their job search timeline
heuristics.action: Redirect all job search energy toward internship applications at H-1B-sponsoring companies rather than full-time new grad applications
heuristics.because: Return offer conversion rates (70–90%) are dramatically higher than cold full-time application conversion rates (1–5%), and the internship pipeline creates an implicit sponsorship commitment before H-1B lottery is even relevant

heuristics.rule: Separate the visa sponsorship decision from the salary negotiation
heuristics.condition: When an employer has already extended an offer that includes H-1B sponsorship...
heuristics.action: ...treat visa confirmation as an operational detail to verify early, then negotiate compensation as a separate conversation with full professional leverage
heuristics.because: The employer has already committed to the cost and risk of sponsorship by making the offer; that decision is made and does not deplete your negotiating capital on salary

heuristics.rule: Apply tech recruiting logic only to tech; each industry has a different sponsorship and recruiting structure
heuristics.condition: When an international student is job searching in finance, consulting, biotech, or policy...
heuristics.action: ...use industry-specific sponsorship data, recruiting calendars, and target employer lists rather than generic international student advice
heuristics.because: Most international student job search advice is implicitly written for tech, producing systematically wrong guidance when applied to other industries

heuristics.rule: Start internship search 9–12 months before start date; start full-time search 6–12 months before graduation; for international students on OPT, start 12–18 months before graduation
heuristics.condition: When planning your job search timeline...
heuristics.action: ...anchor your start date to your target end date and work backward, treating job search as a concurrent multi-semester project rather than a post-graduation task
heuristics.because: By the time urgency is felt, the best options (early referrals, relationship-building cycles, insider knowledge) have already been foreclosed

heuristics.rule: Target hiring managers who have been in their role less than 2 years
heuristics.condition: When doing cold outreach to managers at a target company...
heuristics.action: ...prioritize contacts who are relatively new to their role over long-tenured managers
heuristics.because: Newer managers are more receptive to outreach, likely still building their teams and less entrenched in existing hiring pipelines

heuristics.rule: Filter companies for sponsorship willingness before applying, not after investing emotionally in the process
heuristics.condition: When you are an international student beginning your job search...
heuristics.action: ...use USCIS H-1B disclosure data, Handshake filters, and alumni networks to build a target list of proven sponsors before sending a single application
heuristics.because: Discovering a company doesn't sponsor after 3+ interview rounds is a preventable failure that wastes time and creates false hope

heuristics.rule: During PGWP, tell employers 'I have open work authorization — no sponsorship required' rather than disclosing visa status framing
heuristics.condition: When a PGWP holder is in job search mode and an employer asks about work authorization...
heuristics.action: ...frame it as 'I have a 3-year open work permit valid until [date], no sponsorship required,' and proactively mention the PR pathway
heuristics.because: PGWP is legally equivalent to domestic work authorization for employers — framing it as a 'visa issue' creates false hesitation that doesn't exist

heuristics.rule: Look up the NOC code of any target role before accepting it, not after
heuristics.condition: When evaluating a job offer or targeting a role as a PGWP holder
heuristics.action: Confirm the NOC TEER classification independently — do not rely on the employer's job title or description to infer CEC eligibility
heuristics.because: Misclassified roles where employer calls it technical but NOC codes it as administrative have caused CEC eligibility rejections; a 'Junior IT Analyst' might be TEER 2 not TEER 1 — both eligible, but the distinction must be known before acceptance

heuristics.rule: Keep cold emails to 50–120 words maximum
heuristics.condition: When drafting any unsolicited outreach message...
heuristics.action: ...cut everything that isn't specific common ground, one proof of relevance, or the ask — if it exceeds 150 words, the receiver stops reading
heuristics.because: Message length above 150 words is a reliable failure signal; brevity signals respect for the recipient's time and forces you to be specific

heuristics.rule: Match outreach target to company size
heuristics.condition: When deciding who to cold email at a company...
heuristics.action: ...contact CEO/CTO at <30 person companies, technical recruiters at mid-size, university recruiters at 750+ employee companies, and never target Directors or VPs
heuristics.because: Contact point relevance varies by org structure; too-senior contacts lack operational hiring authority and are harder to reach meaningfully

heuristics.rule: If a company offers H-1B sponsorship without being able to describe specific job duties, SOC code, wage level, and worksite, the petition is likely fraudulent
heuristics.condition: When a potential sponsor cannot articulate exactly what work you will do before filing...
heuristics.action: ...decline the offer, because the H-1B will be filed with incorrect or fabricated information
heuristics.because: Legitimate H-1B sponsorship requires a specific job with specific details; vagueness means the employer is either misrepresenting the role or filing fraudulently

heuristics.rule: For international students with OPT deadlines, start full-time job search 12-18 months before graduation
heuristics.condition: When you are an international student with visa authorization constraints...
heuristics.action: ...begin company targeting, network activation, and outreach 12-18 months before graduation rather than treating it as a post-graduation task
heuristics.because: Visa timelines compress options; by the time urgency is felt, the best relationship-building windows have already closed

heuristics.rule: Never lead a networking conversation with your visa status or sponsorship need
heuristics.condition: When initiating contact with a recruiter, hiring manager, or professional connection...
heuristics.action: ...lead with your value proposition and only address sponsorship when directly asked or when an offer is imminent
heuristics.because: Opening with a constraint frames you as a liability before you have established value; sponsorship becomes secondary once the employer wants you

heuristics.rule: Never exceed 11 months of full-time CPT without consulting your DSO
heuristics.condition: When an international student is considering a long-term or sequential CPT-based internship
heuristics.action: Track cumulative full-time CPT usage across all positions and stop before hitting 12 months total
heuristics.because: 12 cumulative months of full-time CPT permanently eliminates OPT eligibility — this is irreversible and closes the primary US work authorization pathway for that degree level

heuristics.rule: Confirm visa sponsorship before negotiating salary, not after
heuristics.condition: When receiving an offer as an international student who needs H-1B sponsorship...
heuristics.action: ...first confirm sponsorship is in place as a matter-of-fact operational check, then pivot immediately to salary negotiation
heuristics.because: Negotiating salary before confirming sponsorship risks investing negotiating energy in an offer that can't materialize; doing it after confirmation means you're negotiating from a position of mutual commitment

heuristics.rule: Target bulge-bracket banks and large asset managers for finance sponsorship; avoid boutiques unless verified
heuristics.condition: When an international student is pursuing investment banking or asset management...
heuristics.action: ...prioritize Goldman Sachs, JPMorgan, Morgan Stanley, Citi, BofA, Barclays, Deutsche Bank and large asset managers over middle-market or boutique firms
heuristics.because: Middle-market banks sponsor inconsistently and boutique investment banks (10–30 people) often do not sponsor at all

heuristics.rule: Allocate 50%+ of job search time to cold outreach and referral requests, not to applications or resume polishing
heuristics.condition: When deciding how to spend your daily job search hours...
heuristics.action: ...prioritize Type A activities (cold outreach, referral requests, networking with strangers) over Type B (applying to postings) and Type C (browsing, optimizing resume abstractly)
heuristics.because: Type A has the highest return per hour invested even though response rates per message are low; Type C feels productive but generates zero pipeline

heuristics.rule: Keep cold emails to 50–125 words maximum
heuristics.condition: When writing a cold email to a hiring manager or potential referrer...
heuristics.action: ...ruthlessly cut everything that isn't common ground, proof of worth, or a specific ask
heuristics.because: Longer emails signal lack of respect for the recipient's time and reduce response rates; brevity forces clarity and prioritization

heuristics.rule: Lead with value, not visa status, in every networking interaction
heuristics.condition: When initiating contact with a potential employer or professional contact...
heuristics.action: ...open with your skills, interests, and what you bring — never open with 'I need visa sponsorship'
heuristics.because: Leading with a constraint frames you as a liability; leading with value lets sponsorship become secondary to your candidacy

heuristics.rule: If a tech role qualifies for Global Talent Stream Category B, tell employers the sponsorship burden is 2 weeks, not months
heuristics.condition: When negotiating post-PGWP work authorization with a tech employer who is unfamiliar with GTS...
heuristics.action: ...explicitly state that GTS processing takes 2 weeks and requires no LMIA for eligible occupations, and name the category
heuristics.because: Employer hesitation about post-PGWP sponsorship is often based on conflating it with normal LMIA (3-6 months); GTS removes the objection entirely for eligible roles

heuristics.rule: Pursue Provincial Nomination before any other CRS optimization lever post-March 2025
heuristics.condition: When trying to maximize CRS score after LMIA job offer points were removed
heuristics.action: Target PNP streams first — a single nomination adds 600 CRS points and functionally guarantees an ITA regardless of base CRS score
heuristics.because: No other single action comes close to the 600-point PNP bonus; all other levers (French, additional work experience, education) add at most 25-100 points each

heuristics.rule: Send the referral ask 2–4 weeks after the informational call, not during it
heuristics.condition: When you've had a genuine first informational interview and a relevant role has opened...
heuristics.action: ...wait until the second touch to ask for a referral, framing it as 'I wanted to ask if you'd be open to' rather than 'can you'
heuristics.because: The social obligation that makes a referral feel natural takes time to form; asking too early before that obligation exists feels transactional and gets declined

heuristics.rule: Keep cold emails between 50–125 words
heuristics.condition: When writing a cold outreach email to a hiring manager...
heuristics.action: ...cut everything that doesn't establish common ground, proof of worth, or a specific ask
heuristics.because: Longer emails signal poor communication skills and reduce read-through rates; brevity forces prioritization of only the strongest signals

heuristics.rule: If an H-1B sponsorship offer arrives within days of a first conversation with a firm you don't know, treat it as a red flag, not a win
heuristics.condition: When sponsorship is offered extremely fast before any real vetting of your role...
heuristics.action: ...slow down and conduct due diligence rather than accepting out of relief or urgency
heuristics.because: Legitimate sponsors have internal approval processes and established attorney relationships; speed signals the offer is not grounded in a real role

heuristics.rule: The further down the referral priority list you are, the more proof of worth must be in your outreach message
heuristics.condition: When reaching out to someone at a target company with no close connection...
heuristics.action: ...front-load your outreach with concrete evidence of your work and value rather than relying on the connection itself to carry weight
heuristics.because: A cold contact with no obvious common ground has no social obligation to help; demonstrated worth is the substitute for relationship

heuristics.rule: Disclose visa status matter-of-factly and reframe it as mutual benefit, not a burden
heuristics.condition: When a recruiter asks about work authorization during early screening...
heuristics.action: ...respond directly with your OPT end date and frame long-term commitment as the value exchange: 'visa holders don't job-hop casually'
heuristics.because: Apologetic or evasive framing signals that sponsorship is a problem; confident framing signals it is a manageable, worthwhile investment for the employer

heuristics.rule: Any company you target for internship must have filed 10+ H-1B applications per year in recent years
heuristics.condition: When evaluating whether to invest time applying to a company as an international student
heuristics.action: Check H1Bdata.info or MyVisaJobs.com before applying; exclude companies with fewer than 5 annual H-1B filings
heuristics.because: A company that doesn't sponsor full-time employees won't sponsor you after the internship — filtering upfront prevents wasted internship investment

heuristics.rule: If base salary is firm, redirect to signing bonus
