decision_factors.factor: Degree level (master's/PhD vs. bachelor's vs. other)
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Determines both PGWP duration and whether field of study eligibility rules apply
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Master's and PhD graduates receive automatic 3-year PGWP and are exempt from field of study requirements. Bachelor's graduates must meet field of study criteria. Other program graduates receive PGWP equal to program length (if 8 months to under 2 years) or 3 years (if 2 years or longer).

decision_factors.factor: Employer type (direct-hire vs. IT consulting/outsourcing vs. staffing)
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Employer category is the single strongest predictor of H-1B approval rate in FY2025 data, with a spread of over 37 percentage points between best and worst categories
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Check employer against category benchmarks: direct-hire Fortune 100 tech (97.4% approval), IT consulting/outsourcing (78.2% approval), small companies <50 employees (65–80% approval), IT staffing firms (60–75% approval)

decision_factors.factor: Field of study (bachelor's level graduates only)
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Determines whether a bachelor's graduate is eligible for a PGWP at all under post-November 1, 2024 rules
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Check whether the program appears on the IRCC-approved eligible fields list. 178 fields including many general business, liberal arts, and some social science programs were removed effective November 1, 2024.

decision_factors.factor: Third-party placement at client site
decision_factors.why_it_matters: USCIS identifies third-party placement as the single biggest red flag in H-1B adjudications, driving elevated RFE and denial rates across all IT staffing and body-shop consulting arrangements
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Determine whether the H-1B worker will be working at the sponsoring employer's own location or placed at a third-party client site

decision_factors.factor: Program start date relative to November 1, 2024
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Determines whether transitional protection applies for bachelor's students in fields removed from PGWP eligibility
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Students who started before November 1, 2024 in an affected program may have transitional protection; students who started on or after that date in a removed field are not eligible

decision_factors.factor: DOL Wage Level filed (I through IV)
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Level I filings face RFE rates 5x higher than Level IV filings (34.2% vs. 6.8%); USCIS scrutinizes lower-wage positions as potentially not qualifying as specialty occupations
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Identify which DOL wage level the employer is certifying on the LCA: Level I (~17th percentile, entry-level), Level II (some experience), Level III (experienced), Level IV (~67th percentile, fully competent independent judgment)

decision_factors.factor: NOC TEER level of Canadian employment
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Determines whether work experience counts toward CEC eligibility in Express Entry
decision_factors.how_to_assess: TEER 0, 1, 2, or 3 = CEC-eligible. TEER 4 or 5 = not CEC-eligible, even if full-time and legally authorized under PGWP.

decision_factors.factor: Employer petition volume
decision_factors.why_it_matters: High-volume employers (e.g., Amazon: 4,644 approvals; Meta: 1,555; Microsoft: 1,394; Google: 1,050) demonstrate established H-1B infrastructure and consistent USCIS processing relationships
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Check USCIS H-1B Employer Data Hub for number of new H-1B petitions approved in FY2025

decision_factors.factor: Timing of PGWP application relative to study permit expiry
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Determines whether the graduate can work legally during the approximately 8-month PGWP processing period
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Application must be submitted before the study permit expires to access maintained status work authorization during processing

decision_factors.factor: Advanced degree (US Master's or higher)
decision_factors.why_it_matters: 20,000 of the 85,000 annual H-1B cap slots are reserved exclusively for US advanced degree holders, increasing selection probability relative to the general cap pool
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Confirm whether applicant holds a US Master's degree or higher to determine eligibility for the Master's cap exemption within the lottery

decision_factors.factor: French language proficiency (TEF Canada or TCF Canada)
decision_factors.why_it_matters: French language bonus remains in effect in CRS and is now one of the most impactful CRS optimizations available following removal of LMIA job offer points
decision_factors.how_to_assess: TEF Canada or TCF Canada scores can add 25-50+ CRS points

decision_factors.factor: RFE rate of sponsoring employer
decision_factors.why_it_matters: A high RFE rate (e.g., Cognizant 38.8%, TCS ~37%) indicates a pattern of USCIS scrutiny that extends processing time, increases legal costs, and creates uncertainty even before a final denial decision
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Check employer RFE rate via USCIS H-1B Employer Data Hub or H1B Data Hub analysis; compare against category benchmarks (direct-hire tech: 6.1%, IT consulting: 38.8%)

decision_factors.factor: Provincial Nominee Program (PNP) eligibility
decision_factors.why_it_matters: A provincial nomination adds 600 CRS points, guaranteeing an Invitation to Apply (ITA), and is more important now that LMIA job offer points are removed
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Assess alignment with specific PNP stream requirements for the candidate's occupation, work location, and province

decision_factors.factor: Cap-exempt status of employer
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Cap-exempt employers (universities, affiliated research institutions, government research organizations, nonprofit research organizations) are not subject to the 85,000 annual cap or lottery, eliminating the ~64.7% rejection rate from the lottery process
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Determine whether the employer qualifies as a university, affiliated research institution, government research organization, or nonprofit research organization under USCIS definitions

decision_factors.factor: Core CRS factors: language (CLB/IELTS), education, age, Canadian work experience
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Following the removal of LMIA job offer points, these core factors are the primary determinants of CRS score
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Candidates compete purely on these factors without the ability to supplement via arranged employment LMIA route

decision_factors.factor: TEER level of current or target employment
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Determines whether work experience counts toward Canadian Experience Class PR eligibility — the most common PR pathway for PGWP holders
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Look up the NOC code for your role on the IRCC NOC database and confirm whether it is classified TEER 0, 1, 2, or 3 (eligible) versus TEER 4 or 5 (not eligible for CEC)

decision_factors.factor: Employer cap-exempt status
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Determines whether the candidate must survive a 35% annual lottery or can receive H-1B approval with certainty
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Check whether employer is a university, non-profit research organization, or government research entity — these categories are explicitly exempt from the 85,000 annual cap

decision_factors.factor: French language proficiency level
decision_factors.why_it_matters: French CLB 7+ unlocks dedicated Express Entry draws with cut-offs 80-120 points below general draws, dramatically changing the feasibility timeline for PR
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Take a diagnostic TEF Canada or TCF Canada practice test; assess gap between current level and CLB 7 threshold; estimate time investment required to reach it

decision_factors.factor: Employer H-1B petition volume
decision_factors.why_it_matters: High-volume filers have established immigration compliance infrastructure; low-volume or first-time filers introduce legal uncertainty and processing risk
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Search employer petition history on H1BData.info; employers with 100+ annual petitions have demonstrated compliance infrastructure; first-time filers have higher procedural risk

decision_factors.factor: PGWP duration remaining
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Time remaining on PGWP determines how much CEC-eligible experience can be accumulated before needing to either obtain PR or secure employer-sponsored status
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Calculate months remaining; determine if enough time exists to accumulate the 1 year of TEER 0-3 experience required for CEC before permit expiry

decision_factors.factor: Country of birth relative to green card backlog
decision_factors.why_it_matters: India and China nationals face 50+ year green card backlogs; all other nationalities face 5–15 years — this fundamentally changes whether US-only strategy is viable long-term
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Check USCIS Visa Bulletin for current priority dates by country and employment-based category; compare against Canadian Express Entry processing time of 18–30 months for the same profile

decision_factors.factor: Province of residence and employer location
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Provincial variation in PNP streams, CRS cut-offs, cost of living, and sector concentration significantly changes the feasibility and speed of different PR pathways
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Map current location to available PNP streams; compare BC PNP Tech, OINP, QSWP, and prairie province programs against your NOC code and education level

decision_factors.factor: Company size relative to sponsorship cost burden
decision_factors.why_it_matters: For a 30-person startup, $10,000 per sponsorship is a real budget constraint; for a large employer it is negligible — this predicts actual sponsorship willingness
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Estimate headcount and funding stage; seed/Series A startups under 50 people are highest risk for sponsorship refusal due to cost; companies over 500 employees rarely decline on cost grounds alone

decision_factors.factor: Education level (bachelor's vs. master's vs. PhD)
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Directly affects CRS score (120/135/140 points respectively) and PGWP duration (master's and PhD typically receive 3-year PGWPs vs. shorter for bachelor's)
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Identify your CRS education points; check PGWP duration issued on your permit; determine if OINP Masters Graduate stream is available to you

decision_factors.factor: H-1B denial and RFE trend for the specific employer
decision_factors.why_it_matters: An employer with a history of RFEs or denials signals either non-compliance, body shop patterns, or weak petition quality — all of which increase personal immigration risk
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Search employer-specific denial and RFE rates on public LCA/H-1B data tools; NFAP data shows overall denial rate is 5.8% but varies significantly by employer type

decision_factors.factor: Employer awareness of open work permit rules
decision_factors.why_it_matters: 22% of employers misunderstand PGWP — they may self-eliminate as hiring options before the candidate has a chance to clarify, artificially shrinking the opportunity pool
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Listen for phrases like 'we don't sponsor' or 'immigration compliance concerns' in early screening; treat these as education opportunities rather than hard rejections

decision_factors.factor: Geographic location relative to H-1B wage levels
decision_factors.why_it_matters: LCA prevailing wage requirements vary by metro; Bay Area wages run 30–50% above national H-1B median — location determines both compensation floor and market competitiveness
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Cross-reference role title and level against DOL LCA public data for the specific metro area at H1BData.info before evaluating any offer

decision_factors.factor: Field of study alignment with employment sector
decision_factors.why_it_matters: PGWP holders disproportionately end up in TEER 4/5 retail and food service roles that do not align with their education — field alignment predicts whether TEER 0-3 employment is achievable without sector transition
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Assess whether your degree directly maps to TEER 0-3 occupations in demand; check whether your sector has dedicated Express Entry category-based draws (STEM, healthcare)

decision_factors.factor: Current OPT/STEM OPT remaining time
decision_factors.why_it_matters: The number of H-1B lottery attempts available before OPT expires determines how much risk a candidate can absorb; a student with one lottery attempt left has no margin for error
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Calculate remaining OPT months, determine how many April lottery cycles remain, and model worst-case scenarios if cap-subject H-1B is not obtained

decision_factors.factor: CRS score relative to current draw cut-offs
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Determines which Express Entry streams you are competitive in and which optimization levers (language, experience, PNP) will yield the most points most quickly
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Calculate your current CRS score using the official IRCC tool; compare to recent general draw cut-offs (480-520), French-language draw cut-offs (365-400), and occupation-specific draw cut-offs

decision_factors.factor: PGWP duration (1 vs. 3 years)
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Determines whether PR can be obtained before open work authorization expires — a 1-year PGWP creates a dangerous gap window; a 3-year PGWP provides enough runway for CEC eligibility and PR processing
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Calculate: program length → PGWP duration → subtract 1 year to CEC eligibility → add 6-12 months for PR processing → compare to PGWP expiry date

decision_factors.factor: PGWP remaining duration
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Determines how much time exists to complete Phase 1 (get TEER-eligible role) and Phase 2 (accumulate 12 months, apply CEC) before status expires
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Calculate months remaining on PGWP; subtract 12 months needed for CEC work experience; the remainder is the maximum Phase 1 job search window

decision_factors.factor: Who you are targeting (executive vs. manager)
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Executives rarely respond to cold outreach; managers — especially newer ones — have higher response rates and more direct hiring influence
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Check LinkedIn title, seniority level, and years in current role; filter for people 1–2 levels above the role you want, not C-suite

decision_factors.factor: Strength of proof of worth
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Cold emails only convert if the background behind them is respond-worthy; the email opens the door but the background determines if you walk through
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Inventory your portfolio: measurable project outcomes, hackathon placements, OSS adoption, quantified internship results, school or employer prestige

decision_factors.factor: Whether employer pays all H-1B fees without exception
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Charging workers for fees is illegal and is the clearest single indicator of a fraudulent or non-compliant arrangement
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Ask directly and in writing whether you will be charged any fees related to the H-1B petition, filing, or legal process

decision_factors.factor: Referral proximity to target company
decision_factors.why_it_matters: The closeness of your connection to someone at a company determines how much proof of worth your outreach must carry and how likely the referral is to result in human resume review
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Map your LinkedIn and personal network against each target company; categorize each contact as close friend, acquaintance, mutual connection, or cold contact

decision_factors.factor: Company sponsorship track record
decision_factors.why_it_matters: A company's historical H-1B filing and approval rate predicts whether they have the process, legal support, and institutional willingness to sponsor — intention alone is insufficient
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Search H1Bdata.info and MyVisaJobs.com for the company's H-1B petition history and approval rates; cross-reference with alumni network intel

decision_factors.factor: Company H-1B filing history
decision_factors.why_it_matters: A company's past H-1B filings predict whether they will sponsor you after the internship; without this, the entire internship-to-return-offer strategy fails at the visa stage
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Search H1Bdata.info and MyVisaJobs.com by company name; look at volume of annual filings over recent years; flag companies under 5/year as high risk

decision_factors.factor: Whether employer has already committed to H-1B sponsorship
decision_factors.why_it_matters: If sponsorship is already embedded in the offer, the fear-based reason to avoid negotiating is eliminated — the decision is made and salary is now a separate variable
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Confirm explicitly during offer stage: 'I'll need H-1B sponsorship starting [date] — is that process confirmed on your end?'

decision_factors.factor: Industry-specific sponsorship reliability
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Sponsorship rates differ dramatically by industry — applying the same strategy across industries produces wrong outcomes
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Cross-reference USCIS H-1B petition data for specific employers in the target industry; consult the industry comparison matrix

decision_factors.factor: Position in the referral chain
decision_factors.why_it_matters: A close friend who can vouch for you personally creates a fundamentally different social obligation than a cold contact with no common ground; the conversion rate and required effort differ dramatically across the five levels
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Map each target company contact against the five-tier referral hierarchy: (1) close friend who vouches, (2) acquaintance who knows your reputation, (3) mutual connection who forwards, (4) cold contact with common ground, (5) cold contact with no connection

decision_factors.factor: Proof of worth before outreach
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Cold emails only work if there is respond-worthy content backing them; without accomplishments, even perfectly written emails fail because the email opens the door but the background walks through it
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Check whether you have at least one of: portfolio projects with measurable outcomes, hackathon wins, OSS contributions with adoption metrics, published work, quantified internship achievements, or prestigious school/employer names

decision_factors.factor: Company H-1B filing history and approval rate
decision_factors.why_it_matters: A company's past sponsorship behavior is the most reliable predictor of whether they will sponsor you — stated willingness without a track record is high risk
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Search H1Bdata.info and MyVisaJobs.com using the company name; check number of petitions filed and approval rate over recent years

decision_factors.factor: Role eligibility for Global Talent Stream Category B
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Determines post-PGWP employer sponsorship burden — GTS Category B reduces it to 2 weeks vs. 3-6 months for standard LMIA, making employer willingness to sponsor dramatically higher
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Check if your NOC code appears on the Global Talent Occupations List published by ESDC; confirm role matches the listed occupation description

decision_factors.factor: NOC TEER classification of target roles
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Only TEER 0/1/2/3 work experience qualifies for CEC; TEER 4/5 does not count regardless of how skilled or technical the role feels
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Look up the specific NOC code on the IRCC NOC finder before accepting any offer; do not rely on employer job title to infer classification

decision_factors.factor: Specificity of the connection hook
decision_factors.why_it_matters: A generic opener signals mass outreach and triggers deletion; a specific reference to something the person did recently signals genuine interest
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Ask: could this opening line have been sent to 100 other people? If yes, it's too generic — find something specific: a post, talk, article, or mutual contact

decision_factors.factor: Hiring manager tenure at current role
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Managers newer to their role are more receptive to outreach and more actively building teams
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Check LinkedIn for start date in current role; prioritize contacts with under 2 years in position

decision_factors.factor: Specificity of the job role before petition filing
decision_factors.why_it_matters: H-1B petitions require specific job duties, SOC codes, and worksites; vagueness predicts a fraudulent petition that can harm your immigration record
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Ask the employer to describe the exact position, SOC code they intend to file under, and the specific worksite location before agreeing to anything

decision_factors.factor: Work authorization timeline and visa status
decision_factors.why_it_matters: For international students, OPT and visa deadlines impose hard constraints on when job search must begin and which companies are viable targets; mismanaging this forecloses options entirely
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Know the exact dates of authorization windows; have a written communication ready to share with recruiters proactively

decision_factors.factor: Company size and immigration infrastructure
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Large companies have dedicated immigration teams and established processes; small companies may sponsor in principle but fail in execution, resulting in lost job offers or failed petitions
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Ask directly whether they have in-house immigration counsel or use an external firm; look for evidence of repeat H-1B filings in public data

decision_factors.factor: Cumulative full-time CPT usage
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Crossing 12 cumulative months permanently eliminates OPT — the single most damaging and irreversible authorization error an international student can make
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Track all CPT authorization periods across all employers and internships; consult DSO before accepting any position that would push total near or over 11 months

decision_factors.factor: Whether employer uses standardized pay bands
decision_factors.why_it_matters: At large companies with rigid pay bands, base salary negotiation has a structural ceiling; knowing this redirects effort to signing bonus, equity, and job level rather than base
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Ask directly if the offer is within a fixed pay band; research company size and HR structure; tech companies with 1000+ employees typically have bands

decision_factors.factor: Company size within the industry
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Even in sponsorship-friendly industries, small companies (under 50 people in tech, boutiques in finance/consulting) often cannot or do not sponsor
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Check USCIS historical petition data; ask directly whether the company has previously sponsored H-1B and who handled immigration

decision_factors.factor: Timing relative to need
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Networking done 12+ months before graduation yields authentic conversations, reciprocal relationships, and discovery of unknown opportunities; networking done in desperation is detectable and limited to only what is currently available
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Calculate months remaining before your target start date or OPT authorization deadline and compare against recommended lead times (9–12 months for internships, 12–18 months for international students)

decision_factors.factor: Outreach channel selection
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Online applications succeed at 4–10% rates while direct outreach achieves 25–50% response rates with personalization; channel choice determines how much of the opportunity set you actually access
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Determine what proportion of your current job search effort is going to job boards versus direct outreach versus referral acquisition

decision_factors.factor: Company size and immigration infrastructure
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Large companies have dedicated immigration teams and established processes; small companies may have good intentions but fail at execution, leaving the candidate stranded
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Ask directly in later interview stages whether they have an immigration attorney on retainer and how many H-1B employees they currently have

decision_factors.factor: Province of job offer relative to PNP stream eligibility
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Provincial nomination can add 600 CRS points, essentially guaranteeing PR invitation — the province of employment determines which PNP streams are accessible
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Check BC Tech Pilot, OINP Masters Graduate stream, AAIP, and SINP eligibility criteria against your NOC code, education, and job offer details; compare processing times across provinces

decision_factors.factor: Province of study and residence
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Determines PNP stream eligibility — OINP Masters Graduate requires Ontario degree, SINP Graduate requires Saskatchewan institution, BC PNP requires BC job offer
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Match your degree-granting institution's province to available PNP streams; check whether streams require job offer or are nomination-only

decision_factors.factor: Whether a mutual contact exists
decision_factors.why_it_matters: A name-drop from a shared connection fundamentally changes response probability and the social dynamic of the conversation
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Check LinkedIn second-degree connections; ask existing contacts who they know at target companies before sending cold messages

decision_factors.factor: Company size
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Determines the correct contact tier for outreach; wrong contact level wastes effort and reduces response probability
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Check LinkedIn employee count or Crunchbase; categorize as <30, mid-size, or 750+

decision_factors.factor: Verifiable H-1B petition history of the employer
decision_factors.why_it_matters: A company that claims to sponsor regularly but has no public record of petitions is misrepresenting itself
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Cross-reference company name on H-1Bdata.info, MyVisaJobs.com, and USCIS public employer data

decision_factors.factor: Planning horizon relative to graduation or OPT deadline
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Starting too late makes Type A high-leverage activities impossible because there is no time to build real relationships before you need them
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Count months remaining before graduation or authorization deadline; if less than 6 months, options are already constrained and strategy must shift

decision_factors.factor: OPT and STEM OPT timeline alignment with job start
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Non-negotiable immigration deadlines mean a student's available work window is fixed; misalignment with an employer's hiring cycle can make an otherwise good offer unworkable
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Map OPT start date, OPT expiration, STEM extension eligibility, and H-1B registration window against each employer's typical hiring and onboarding timeline

decision_factors.factor: OPT + STEM OPT timeline relative to H-1B lottery dates
decision_factors.why_it_matters: The gap between graduation, OPT start, H-1B lottery (March), and H-1B effective date (October 1) determines how long an employer must bridge you — employers who can't or won't bridge that gap effectively cannot hire you
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Map your expected graduation date to the OPT start window, then trace forward to the first possible H-1B lottery and effective date; verify the target company has retained employees through lottery cycles

decision_factors.factor: Presence of a competing offer
decision_factors.why_it_matters: A competing offer is the single most powerful negotiating lever available regardless of visa status, because it provides objective external market validation
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Evaluate whether you have a legitimate offer at a different salary level that you can credibly cite; you do not need to disclose the company name

decision_factors.factor: STEM OPT eligibility of the degree
decision_factors.why_it_matters: STEM OPT extends work authorization to 3 years, dramatically changing the risk profile for employers and providing more time before H-1B dependency
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Check whether the degree program is on the DHS STEM OPT designated degree program list; finance degrees are less often STEM-designated than CS or engineering

decision_factors.factor: Work authorization clarity and timeline
decision_factors.why_it_matters: International students have a hard constraint (OPT deadline) that compresses all other timelines and must be proactively communicated to recruiters; failure to manage this creates last-minute scrambles with no recovery options
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Know the exact date of authorization expiration, whether sponsorship is required and when, and whether each target company has a history of sponsoring the relevant visa type

decision_factors.factor: Referral versus cold application
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Referrals lead to 55% faster hiring pipeline and referred candidates are 7–15x more likely to be hired; the structural difference is ATS elimination and priority human review
decision_factors.how_to_assess: For each target company, identify whether you have a warm connection, a school alumni, a former employer overlap, or must go fully cold

decision_factors.factor: OPT and STEM OPT timeline relative to job search start date
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Non-negotiable immigration deadlines create hard constraints on when you need an offer — missing them has severe consequences domestic candidates don't face
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Map your OPT start date, STEM extension eligibility, and H-1B October 1 start date against your graduation and job search timeline

decision_factors.factor: French language proficiency
decision_factors.why_it_matters: French proficiency adds 25-50 CRS points — in competitive Express Entry draws where margins are small, this can be the difference between receiving an ITA or not
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Evaluate current French ability honestly; calculate potential CRS score increase from TEF/TCF scores using the IRCC CRS calculator

decision_factors.factor: French language proficiency or willingness to develop it
decision_factors.why_it_matters: French CLB 7+ unlocks dedicated Francophone draws at cut-offs ~100+ points lower than general draws and adds 25-50 direct CRS points
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Assess current French level; estimate time to CLB 7 on TEF Canada; calculate CRS point gain versus time investment against PGWP timeline

decision_factors.factor: Visa/sponsorship status transparency
decision_factors.why_it_matters: For international students, proactively framing OPT status and researching sponsorship track records avoids wasting outreach on companies that won't sponsor
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Reference OPT authorization directly in the outreach message while simultaneously positioning the company as one known for sponsoring international talent — signals self-awareness and does pre-qualification

decision_factors.factor: Existence of genuine common ground with target contact
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Personalization based on real shared context (same school, same employer, shared interests) dramatically increases referral and cold email response rates
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Review contact's LinkedIn, blog posts, open-source contributions, public writing, and shared alumni networks before writing

decision_factors.factor: Bench period pay policy
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Not paying during non-placement periods violates 20 CFR 655.731 and signals both legal non-compliance and financial instability of the sponsor
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Ask explicitly: 'What is your policy on pay during periods between client placements?' and get it in writing

decision_factors.factor: Quality and completeness of portfolio and proof of work
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Demonstrated outcomes rather than experience descriptions are what hiring managers report as distinguishing hired candidates; without published proof of work, outreach and applications lack credibility
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Assess whether your resume and portfolio contain quantified outcomes (e.g., reduced latency by 40%) or only activity descriptions (e.g., worked on backend systems)

decision_factors.factor: Cap-exempt employer status
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Universities, university-affiliated nonprofits, and government research orgs are exempt from the H-1B lottery, offering the highest immigration stability and no random exclusion risk
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Check whether the organization qualifies as a cap-exempt entity; weigh against typically lower compensation and slower career growth

decision_factors.factor: Internship-to-return-offer conversion rate at the target company
decision_factors.why_it_matters: A 70–90% return offer rate at large tech companies vs. a lower rate at smaller firms changes the expected value of accepting a particular internship
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Research company-specific intern conversion rates via Glassdoor, LinkedIn alumni, or direct conversations with former interns; treat rates below 60% as materially riskier

decision_factors.factor: Visa type and work authorization status
decision_factors.why_it_matters: PGWP holders in Canada negotiate identically to domestic workers with no sponsorship dynamic; H-1B candidates face an asymmetric fear dynamic that must be consciously reframed
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Identify your current and future work authorization status before entering negotiation to calibrate your actual constraints versus perceived constraints

decision_factors.factor: Recruiting calendar alignment
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Each industry has a different recruiting calendar; applying at the wrong time makes candidates structurally invisible
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Map target industry recruiting windows: finance is August–November (earliest), consulting is September–November, tech is year-round with fall/spring peaks

decision_factors.factor: Ability to articulate outcomes, not just experience
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Hiring managers consistently distinguish candidates who can quantify impact ('reduced latency by 40%') from those who describe activity ('worked on backend systems'); this is a filtering criterion, not a tiebreaker
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Test yourself: can you explain your most impactful project in 90 seconds in a way that makes a non-technical hiring manager want to know more?

decision_factors.factor: Degree of personalization in outreach
decision_factors.why_it_matters: High personalization drives 25–50% response rates versus generic outreach achieving 5–25%; the gap is large enough to treat personalization as a conversion multiplier, not a nice-to-have
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Evaluate whether each email references the specific recipient's work, blog posts, OSS contributions, or public viewpoints — not generic company praise

decision_factors.factor: Cap-exempt vs. cap-subject employer status
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Universities, nonprofits affiliated with universities, and government research organizations bypass the H-1B lottery entirely, eliminating the biggest immigration risk
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Verify nonprofit or university affiliation; confirm cap-exempt status with the employer's HR or immigration counsel

decision_factors.factor: Employment classification (employee vs. independent contractor)
decision_factors.why_it_matters: CEC requires 'employed' work experience — contractor/self-employment income does not qualify, meaning misclassification can silently invalidate PR eligibility accumulation
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Review offer letter classification; confirm T4 employment (not T4A contractor) will be issued; verify the company has an employer CRA account number

decision_factors.factor: Education level (master's vs. bachelor's)
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Master's degree unlocks OINP Masters Graduate stream (no job offer required) — one of the most accessible PNP pathways available
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Confirm degree type and Canadian institution; check OINP eligibility requirements for Masters Graduate stream; apply as soon as eligible

decision_factors.factor: Recency of the target's LinkedIn activity
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Recently active people are more likely to see and respond to messages; inactive profiles are low-yield targets
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Use LinkedIn's 'sort by Activity' filter in People search to surface recently active contacts first

decision_factors.factor: Outreach channel being used
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Online applications yield 4–10% success at best; cold outreach to hiring managers yields 25–50% with high personalization; referrals accelerate pipeline by 55%
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Evaluate what percentage of your current job search activity is portal-based vs. direct outreach vs. referral acquisition

decision_factors.factor: Contract terms including non-compete and liquidated damages clauses
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Unusual financial penalties for resignation are used as leverage to keep workers in exploitative conditions even if technically unenforceable
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Have an independent attorney review any contract before signing; flag any clause requiring payment upon resignation

decision_factors.factor: Company growth and hiring stage
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Companies in active growth have unlisted roles that get filled before posting, making them accessible through the hidden job market in ways that stable or contracting companies are not
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Track funding announcements and hiring announcements for target companies; prioritize outreach to companies in expansion phases

decision_factors.factor: Referral access within target companies
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Job board application conversion rates are under 5%; referrals dramatically increase interview probability and can surface sponsorship-willing hiring managers directly
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Check LinkedIn for first- and second-degree connections at each target company, particularly alumni from your program

decision_factors.factor: Recruiting calendar alignment by industry
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Finance and consulting recruiting closes months before tech; missing the window for one industry cannot be compensated for by applying later in the same cycle
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Map application deadlines by industry for the current recruiting year; confirm whether your graduation year aligns with the intern class being recruited

decision_factors.factor: Whether the role includes equity compensation
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Equity is negotiated separately from base salary and often has more room for movement, providing an additional dimension of negotiation beyond base
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Ask whether the offer includes RSUs or options; if yes, negotiate shares/units, vesting cliff, and schedule as a distinct negotiation track

decision_factors.factor: Cap-exempt vs. cap-subject employer status
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Cap-exempt employers eliminate H-1B lottery risk entirely, which is the single largest source of employment uncertainty for international students
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Determine if employer is a university, affiliated research institution, or nonprofit with primary research/educational purpose

decision_factors.factor: Existing network density at target companies
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Most offers are won at steps 2–4 of the funnel (network activation, outreach, conversation) not at step 5 (application); having zero contacts at a target company means starting from the least efficient entry point
decision_factors.how_to_assess: For each company on your target list, count how many current employees you have spoken to in the last 6 months

decision_factors.factor: Contact seniority fit
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Targeting the wrong seniority level (e.g., VPs instead of Managers) reduces response likelihood because senior leaders are insulated from inbound hiring outreach and lack the operational incentive to respond
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Map company size to the appropriate contact level: CEO/CTO for <30, technical recruiters for mid-size, campus recruiters for 750+, managers as default for direct outreach

decision_factors.factor: Quality and warmth of referral channel
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Referrals convert at dramatically higher rates than cold applications, and for international students, a referral from someone who navigated sponsorship at that company carries additional signal
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Assess whether your connection can make an internal introduction or submit a referral through the ATS — not just mention your name casually

decision_factors.factor: Employer's prior LMIA or GTS sponsorship track record
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Employers with no prior sponsorship experience frequently underestimate complexity, timeline, and cost — offers contingent on novel LMIA processes carry high failure risk
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Ask directly whether the company has sponsored foreign workers before; ask for the name of their immigration law firm; search job postings for prior LMIA-backed roles

decision_factors.factor: Field of study and corresponding NOC codes
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Determines which TEER levels are accessible and how broad or narrow the qualifying role universe is for CEC accumulation
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Map your field to TEER 0/1/2/3 NOC codes using the quick reference; identify whether adjacent lower-TEER roles (e.g., TEER 2) are acceptable fallbacks

decision_factors.factor: The specific ask at the end of the message
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Asking for a job destroys the interaction; asking for 20 minutes on a specific topic has a much higher conversion rate
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Check whether the ask requires any commitment beyond a short conversation — if it does, the ask is too heavy for a cold first message

decision_factors.factor: Volume of outreach attempts
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Job search behaves as a sales funnel; low volume with any strategy produces statistically insufficient results regardless of quality
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Track number of cold emails sent, follow-ups sent, referral requests made, and response rates across companies

decision_factors.factor: Company's ability to name clients and connect you with current H-1B employees
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Legitimate staffing firms have real client relationships and satisfied employees; inability or refusal to provide either suggests the company may be operating on paper only
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Ask to speak with at least one current H-1B employee and ask for general client names; observe whether the firm hesitates or deflects

decision_factors.factor: Specificity of interest in each target company
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Hiring managers consistently identify generic interest as a disqualifying signal; candidates who can reference specific products, tech stack, or recent news convert at higher rates
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Test whether you can articulate a specific reason why this company over a competitor; if you cannot, you have not done sufficient research

decision_factors.factor: Behavioral interview preparation depth
decision_factors.why_it_matters: US hiring weighs cultural fit and behavioral signals heavily, more so than in many home-country hiring contexts; underprepared candidates fail even with strong technical qualifications
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Assess whether you have practiced STAR-format responses for common behavioral questions explicitly, not just conceptually understood the method

decision_factors.factor: Manager relationship quality during internship
decision_factors.why_it_matters: The manager's advocacy is a key variable in whether a return offer is extended — work quality alone is insufficient if the manager is neutral on your intent
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Assess frequency and quality of 1:1 interactions, whether manager has converted previous interns, and whether you have explicitly communicated return interest

decision_factors.factor: Employer size
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Small companies have more flexibility on benefits, PTO, professional development budgets, and remote arrangements than large companies with standardized HR policies
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Assess headcount; companies under ~200 employees typically have more discretionary flexibility on non-salary components

decision_factors.factor: H-1B petition complexity by role type
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Some roles (e.g., finance) face higher RFE/denial rates because the specialty occupation requirement is more contested, creating additional risk even at sponsoring firms
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Research whether the role type has historically faced specialty occupation challenges; finance roles are more contested than software engineering roles

decision_factors.factor: Public visibility and discoverability
decision_factors.why_it_matters: The hidden job market is most accessible to people who are findable — through blog posts, open source, talks, LinkedIn articles; invisibility forecloses inbound opportunities entirely
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Search your own name and relevant skill keywords on LinkedIn and GitHub; assess whether a recruiter searching for your skill set would find you without knowing your name

decision_factors.factor: Outreach volume and follow-up discipline
decision_factors.why_it_matters: The job search functions as a sales funnel where volume and persistence directly determine outcomes; single-touch outreach systematically underperforms because many conversions require three or more contacts
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Track how many contacts you are actively following up with, how many follow-up attempts each has received, and whether you are multi-threading at companies that have gone cold

decision_factors.factor: Resume keyword alignment with ATS filters
decision_factors.why_it_matters: ATS systems filter aggressively on keyword match before any human sees the application; a generic resume fails before it is read
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Compare your resume against the job description using keyword overlap; tailor each application individually

decision_factors.factor: IELTS/CELPIP language score
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Language scores are a directly controllable CRS input — higher scores translate directly to more CRS points and faster PR, unlike age or work experience which are fixed
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Use IRCC CRS calculator to simulate score impact; compare current score to CLB 9-10 benchmarks and calculate point gain from improvement

decision_factors.factor: Base CRS score before optimization
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Determines how far from the current ITA cut-off you are and which optimization levers are worth pursuing
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Use IRCC CRS calculator with current credentials; compare output to recent cut-off history; identify point gap and which levers close it fastest

decision_factors.factor: Follow-up timing and spacing
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Too soon feels aggressive; too late loses momentum — the spacing of follow-ups affects both response rate and how the sender is perceived
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Use 3–4 days for first follow-up, 4–5 days for second, 5–7 days for third — total sequence spans roughly 2 weeks

decision_factors.factor: Quality of referral ask logistics
decision_factors.why_it_matters: A referral request that requires effort from the contact is more likely to be declined; frictionless asks produce higher conversion
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Does your referral ask include resume, LinkedIn, phone number, and a pre-written context sentence the contact can forward with minimal modification?

decision_factors.factor: Time remaining on OPT vs. urgency of accepting any sponsorship
decision_factors.why_it_matters: The comparison is not between a body shop and nothing — it is between a body shop and continued legitimate job searching under OPT; the calculus changes depending on how much OPT time remains
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Calculate actual OPT expiration date including any STEM extension eligibility; determine how many months of runway you have for legitimate searching

decision_factors.factor: LinkedIn profile optimization for recruiter search
decision_factors.why_it_matters: LinkedIn functions as a search engine; inbound recruiter discovery depends on keyword and skill optimization, not narrative quality, creating a distinct optimization target from the resume
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Assess whether your headline, skills section, and keywords match the terms recruiters would use to search for candidates in your target role

decision_factors.factor: GPA and institution recognition for entry-level roles
decision_factors.why_it_matters: For first roles, GPA above 3.5 from a recognized institution still functions as a screening signal, particularly in engineering, research, and quantitative fields
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Check whether target companies include GPA thresholds in job postings; factor in ATS keyword filtering on academic credentials

decision_factors.factor: Competing return offer availability
decision_factors.why_it_matters: A competing return offer is the primary negotiating lever available to international students, where comp is otherwise standardized
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Evaluate whether you have or can realistically obtain a second return offer at a comparable company before accepting the first

decision_factors.factor: H-1B prevailing wage floor
decision_factors.why_it_matters: For sponsored roles, USCIS requires the employer to pay above a regulatory minimum, meaning the first offer is already constrained from below — negotiating upward from that floor is normal and expected
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Research prevailing wage for the role/location using DOL wage data; understand that any sponsored offer already exceeds this floor

decision_factors.factor: Geographic concentration of target industry
decision_factors.why_it_matters: In concentrated industries like biotech, geographic flexibility directly expands the available pool of sponsoring employers
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Identify geographic hubs for the target industry; assess whether candidate is willing to relocate to those hubs

decision_factors.factor: Specificity of company targeting rationale
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Generic interest (applied everywhere, prepared for nowhere) is one of the most common reasons candidates fail to get offers; companies detect and penalize it through interview questions about motivation
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Write one sentence explaining why you want to work at each specific company that could not apply to any other company

decision_factors.factor: Internal referrer motivation
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Employees are financially motivated to refer strong candidates ($2,000–$10,000+ bonuses); understanding this changes how you frame your ask — you are giving them an opportunity, not asking a favor
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Determine whether target company has a referral bonus program; assess whether your request makes it easy for them to say yes with minimal effort

decision_factors.factor: Behavioral interview preparation (STAR method)
decision_factors.why_it_matters: US hiring weighs behavioral interviews and cultural fit more heavily than many candidates' home-country contexts — improvising these answers underperforms explicit preparation
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Evaluate whether you have practiced STAR-structured answers for the most common behavioral prompts, not just thought through them abstractly

decision_factors.factor: Target province's job market conditions
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Phase 1 success depends on actually getting hired; a strong market reduces Phase 1 duration and preserves more PGWP runway
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Compare job posting volume in your NOC code across provinces; assess competition level and whether PNP stream in that province requires a job offer

decision_factors.factor: Specificity of the ask
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Vague asks ('learn more') signal unclear intent and give the contact no concrete action to take; specific asks ('30-minute call in the next two weeks') drive response
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Review your email draft — does the ask specify a format, timeframe, and purpose?

decision_factors.factor: Recency and depth of interview practice
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Interview performance is a perishable skill built through out-loud repetition; candidates who have not practiced with another person in the last two weeks are measurably underprepared
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Check when you last did a live out-loud practice session with another person, not internal mental rehearsal

decision_factors.factor: Networking start timing relative to graduation
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Starting late collapses the available window to build relationships before immigration deadlines create urgency, reducing leverage and optionality
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Calculate how many months before graduation you began consistent outreach and relationship-building; benchmark against the 12–18 month optimal window

decision_factors.factor: Part-time vs. full-time CPT status
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Part-time CPT (≤20 hrs/week) does not count toward the 12-month OPT-elimination threshold, enabling more internship flexibility
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Review CPT authorization letter for hours designation; confirm with DSO whether a given role qualifies as part-time for CPT purposes

decision_factors.factor: Degree level relative to industry norms
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Sponsorship access differs significantly by degree level in some industries — biotech is excellent for PhDs but limited for undergrads
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Research typical credential requirements at target employers; understand whether the role being targeted typically requires a specific degree level

decision_factors.factor: Portfolio and proof of work completeness
decision_factors.why_it_matters: These must be completed before outreach begins; initiating networking without published proof of work wastes the relationship window because you cannot demonstrate capability when asked
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Is your portfolio publicly accessible and does it include work a recruiter or hiring manager could evaluate without asking you for context?

decision_factors.factor: Connection type for referral request
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Warm connections (former colleagues, classmates, mutual contacts) require different messaging and have higher conversion than cold alumni or platform-based contacts; conflating them produces suboptimal results
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Categorize each potential referrer as: former colleague/classmate, LinkedIn alumni match, former company employee, university database contact, or cold platform contact — and calibrate ask accordingly

decision_factors.factor: GPA relative to role type and experience level
decision_factors.why_it_matters: GPA remains a filtering signal for first roles, particularly in quantitative and engineering fields at recognized institutions
decision_factors.how_to_assess: GPA above 3.5 at a recognized institution is worth featuring for first roles; below that or with significant work experience, de-emphasize

decision_factors.factor: Cost of living in target city
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Financial sustainability during job search affects how long a candidate can hold out for TEER-eligible roles versus accepting TEER 4/5 work for income
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Compare salary benchmarks against housing and living costs across Toronto, Vancouver, Montreal, Calgary; Montreal offers best salary-to-cost ratio for tech

decision_factors.factor: Compensation tolerance for immigration stability
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Cap-exempt employers pay 20–40% less than private sector equivalents — candidates must decide whether immigration certainty is worth the pay cut
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Compare compensation ranges at cap-exempt vs. cap-subject employers in the same field; calculate total expected value given lottery odds

decision_factors.factor: Diversity of professional network beyond home-country community
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Networking exclusively within your national community limits exposure to sponsor-friendly employers and referral pipelines outside that community
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Audit your LinkedIn connections and informational interview contacts — what percentage are outside your country-of-origin network

decision_factors.factor: PGWP duration remaining
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Employers — especially smaller ones — may informally factor in how long a candidate can work without any additional action; a 3-year PGWP signals more runway than a 1-year permit and reduces implicit risk perception
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Know your exact PGWP expiry date and be prepared to state the remaining duration clearly; 3-year PGWP (granted for programs of 2+ years) is materially different from shorter durations

hidden_tradeoffs.choice: Delaying PGWP application after graduation
hidden_tradeoffs.unstated_consequence: The approximately 8-month PGWP processing time runs regardless of when the application is submitted; graduates who wait months before applying effectively lose that period from their authorized PGWP term before it is even issued
hidden_tradeoffs.who_it_affects: All PGWP-eligible graduates, particularly those in shorter programs who receive a PGWP equal to program length rather than a fixed 3 years

hidden_tradeoffs.choice: Accepting H-1B sponsorship from an IT consulting or outsourcing firm
hidden_tradeoffs.unstated_consequence: FY2025 data shows 12.7% denial rates and 38.8% RFE rates for IT consulting/outsourcing firms — even a successful petition may face USCIS challenges that delay start dates, increase legal costs, and create status uncertainty during adjudication
hidden_tradeoffs.who_it_affects: International students who accept consulting firm offers as a fallback path to H-1B sponsorship, assuming any sponsorship offer is equivalent

hidden_tradeoffs.choice: Accepting TEER 4 or TEER 5 employment under a PGWP
hidden_tradeoffs.unstated_consequence: Time spent in TEER 4 or 5 work (e.g., retail, food service) is legal and generates income but does not accumulate CEC-eligible Canadian work experience, meaning the PGWP clock runs without building the 1 year of skilled experience required for Canadian Experience Class
hidden_tradeoffs.who_it_affects: PGWP holders who work in retail trade, food services, or accommodation — the top sectors where PGWP holders are employed according to IRCC data

hidden_tradeoffs.choice: Accepting a Level I wage H-1B filing from an employer
hidden_tradeoffs.unstated_consequence: Level I filings face RFE rates of 34.2% — 5x higher than Level IV filings at 6.8% — meaning the employer's cost-saving wage decision directly increases the applicant's immigration risk exposure
hidden_tradeoffs.who_it_affects: Entry-level international students whose employers file at the lowest prevailing wage tier to reduce payroll costs

hidden_tradeoffs.choice: Relying on an LMIA-backed job offer to boost CRS score post-Spring 2025
hidden_tradeoffs.unstated_consequence: IRCC removed all arranged employment CRS points via the LMIA route effective Spring 2025; a valid LMIA-backed offer no longer yields 50 or 200 additional CRS points
hidden_tradeoffs.who_it_affects: Express Entry candidates who planned to use an LMIA job offer as a CRS shortcut, particularly those with lower core CRS scores

hidden_tradeoffs.choice: Relying on the H-1B lottery for work authorization continuity
hidden_tradeoffs.unstated_consequence: FY2025 data shows only a ~35.3% overall selection rate with 442,000 unique beneficiaries competing for 85,000 slots; approximately 300,000–350,000 qualified applicants are blocked annually purely due to cap limitations, not merit
hidden_tradeoffs.who_it_affects: All cap-subject H-1B applicants, particularly those without a backup plan if not selected in the lottery

hidden_tradeoffs.choice: Completing a 1-year master's program in Canada
hidden_tradeoffs.unstated_consequence: Under pre-February 15, 2024 rules, a 1-year master's yielded only a 1-year PGWP. Under the updated rules, it yields a 3-year PGWP — graduates who completed their program before the February 15, 2024 effective date may not benefit from this change
hidden_tradeoffs.who_it_affects: International students who completed 1-year master's programs before February 15, 2024

hidden_tradeoffs.choice: Negotiating salary upward from Level I to Level II or III
hidden_tradeoffs.unstated_consequence: An employer who files at a higher wage level must legally pay that higher wage to comply with DOL prevailing wage requirements — the wage level on the LCA creates a binding legal floor, not just a benchmark
hidden_tradeoffs.who_it_affects: International students who do not realize that their salary negotiation directly affects and is constrained by the DOL LCA wage level filed

hidden_tradeoffs.choice: Enrolling in a bachelor's program in a general business, liberal arts, or certain social science field
hidden_tradeoffs.unstated_consequence: 178 fields including many general business, liberal arts, and some social science programs were removed from PGWP eligibility effective November 1, 2024; bachelor's graduates in these fields are no longer eligible for a PGWP
hidden_tradeoffs.who_it_affects: Bachelor's degree students who started programs in removed fields on or after November 1, 2024

hidden_tradeoffs.choice: Working for a small company (fewer than 50 employees) as H-1B sponsor
hidden_tradeoffs.unstated_consequence: Small companies have approval rates of only 65–80% and denial rates of approximately 15%, significantly below the 97.4% approval rate of Fortune 100 direct-hire tech employers
hidden_tradeoffs.who_it_affects: International students who prioritize role fit, equity, or startup experience without accounting for materially higher H-1B approval risk at small employers

hidden_tradeoffs.choice: Taking any available job quickly after graduation to secure income
hidden_tradeoffs.unstated_consequence: If that job is TEER 4/5 (retail, food service), the CEC clock never starts — a graduate can be legally employed for the full PGWP duration and still be ineligible for the most common PR pathway
hidden_tradeoffs.who_it_affects: Graduates in non-STEM fields, recent arrivals with limited professional networks, and those under financial pressure who cannot afford to wait for skilled employment

hidden_tradeoffs.choice: Joining a prestigious large tech company (top 4 sponsor) for first H-1B
hidden_tradeoffs.unstated_consequence: High employer volume provides sponsorship certainty, but the same employer concentration means layoffs at Amazon/Meta/Microsoft/Google simultaneously flood the H-1B transfer market with thousands of workers, creating intense competition for portability transfers at precisely the moment you need one
hidden_tradeoffs.who_it_affects: H-1B holders at high-volume tech employers during industry downturns or mass layoff cycles

hidden_tradeoffs.choice: Choosing Toronto or Vancouver for post-graduation employment due to largest job markets
hidden_tradeoffs.unstated_consequence: Highest competition for PGWP holders AND highest cost of living, meaning the initial wage gap (10-25% below domestic graduates) is most painful in exactly the cities with the most PGWP holders
hidden_tradeoffs.who_it_affects: Graduates who over-indexed on city prestige and did not model actual take-home pay against local cost of living

hidden_tradeoffs.choice: Accepting H-1B sponsorship from a small startup
hidden_tradeoffs.unstated_consequence: If the startup fails or does a reduction in force before the H-1B is approved, the petition is withdrawn and the worker reverts to OPT status with no backup — small companies also lack in-house immigration counsel, increasing petition error rates
hidden_tradeoffs.who_it_affects: International candidates at early-stage companies who trade compensation upside for sponsorship without modeling downside scenarios

hidden_tradeoffs.choice: Focusing exclusively on accumulating Canadian work experience to improve CRS score
hidden_tradeoffs.unstated_consequence: Ignores French language as a lever — for most PGWP holders, learning French to CLB 7 will yield more CRS points faster than 2-3 additional years of work experience, but requires upfront time investment
hidden_tradeoffs.who_it_affects: Non-Francophone PGWP holders who are stuck just below Express Entry cut-offs and don't realize French is the fastest available optimization

hidden_tradeoffs.choice: Staying in a cap-exempt university research role to avoid lottery risk
hidden_tradeoffs.unstated_consequence: University roles typically pay 20–40% below industry for equivalent skill levels, and the research career track has a narrower exit into industry the longer you stay — the lottery risk is eliminated but compensation and optionality costs compound over time
hidden_tradeoffs.who_it_affects: High-skill international graduates in computer science or engineering who could command $130,000–$160,000 in industry but take $80,000–$100,000 university roles for immigration certainty

hidden_tradeoffs.choice: Staying in Quebec for lower cost of living and French immersion
hidden_tradeoffs.unstated_consequence: Quebec operates an entirely separate immigration system (CSQ/QSWP) — PGWP holders in Quebec cannot use Express Entry CEC directly and must navigate a different process with French proficiency as an effective requirement
hidden_tradeoffs.who_it_affects: Graduates who moved to Montreal for economic reasons without understanding the Quebec immigration system's independence from federal Express Entry

hidden_tradeoffs.choice: Pursuing US-only career strategy as an India or China national
hidden_tradeoffs.unstated_consequence: The H-1B lottery gives 35% annual odds, but surviving the lottery does not solve the problem — the employment-based green card backlog for India nationals can exceed 50 years at current rates, meaning decades of renewal dependency, restrictions on job changes, and inability to start a company without abandoning green card priority dates
hidden_tradeoffs.who_it_affects: India and China nationals who focus on H-1B acquisition as the finish line without modeling the full permanent residency timeline

hidden_tradeoffs.choice: Accepting a lower salary to break into the Canadian labour market
hidden_tradeoffs.unstated_consequence: The initial wage gap is real and documented (10-25%), but graduates who don't plan for it financially risk over-leveraging on debt or housing costs that domestic salary benchmarks would support but their actual salary does not
hidden_tradeoffs.who_it_affects: International graduates who based post-graduation financial plans on domestic graduate salary data rather than actual PGWP holder wage outcomes

hidden_tradeoffs.choice: Negotiating a sponsorship assistance clause where the employee contributes to attorney costs
hidden_tradeoffs.unstated_consequence: While it may unlock sponsorship from a reluctant small employer, paying toward your own H-1B petition creates legal complications, may violate DOL regulations depending on structure, and sets a precedent that immigration costs are employee-borne — requires immigration attorney review before execution
hidden_tradeoffs.who_it_affects: Candidates at small companies with no prior immigration infrastructure who are eager enough to accept financial risk to secure sponsorship

hidden_tradeoffs.choice: Accepting a higher-paying job offer in Ontario over a lower-paying offer in Saskatchewan
hidden_tradeoffs.unstated_consequence: Ontario's competitive OINP pool and higher CRS cut-off scores may delay PR by 2-4 years compared to a Saskatchewan PNP stream where selection is less competitive
hidden_tradeoffs.who_it_affects: PGWP holders with moderate CRS scores (below 470-480) who would not rank highly in federal Express Entry draws but might qualify for provincial streams

hidden_tradeoffs.choice: Spending 6-12 months searching exclusively for an ideal role rather than any qualifying TEER 0/1/2/3 role
hidden_tradeoffs.unstated_consequence: CEC window is compressed or eliminated entirely; candidate must rely on PGWP renewal, alternative streams, or departure from Canada rather than the intended CEC pathway
hidden_tradeoffs.who_it_affects: PGWP holders who job search like domestic graduates without accounting for the immigration timeline running concurrently

hidden_tradeoffs.choice: Asking for a referral during the first informational call
hidden_tradeoffs.unstated_consequence: You collapse the relationship before it forms — the person has no social reason to advocate for someone they just met, and the ask makes the whole interaction feel like it was instrumentally motivated
hidden_tradeoffs.who_it_affects: Job seekers who are under time pressure (e.g., approaching OPT deadline) and feel they can't afford the 2–4 week wait

hidden_tradeoffs.choice: Applying exclusively through online job portals
hidden_tradeoffs.unstated_consequence: You are competing for only 20–30% of available positions; the majority of roles are filled before or without ever being publicly posted
hidden_tradeoffs.who_it_affects: International students and career switchers who default to structured application systems as a perceived safer or more organized approach

hidden_tradeoffs.choice: Accepting body shop H-1B sponsorship to secure immigration status quickly
hidden_tradeoffs.unstated_consequence: Two years in a body shop often produces a weak or uncreditable employment history, a potentially non-compliant immigration record, and difficulty explaining the experience to future legitimate employers
hidden_tradeoffs.who_it_affects: International students near OPT expiration who feel no other option exists and accept out of panic rather than calculation

hidden_tradeoffs.choice: Spending most job search time on application submission and resume optimization
hidden_tradeoffs.unstated_consequence: You are competing in the 10-25% of applicants who survive ATS filtering while simultaneously building no relationships that would bypass that filter; high effort produces low and declining returns
hidden_tradeoffs.who_it_affects: Students who interpret activity volume as progress and conflate feeling productive with generating pipeline

failure_patterns.pattern: Bachelor's graduate applies for PGWP after completing a program in a field removed from eligibility on or after November 1, 2024
failure_patterns.why_it_happens: IRCC removed 178 fields from PGWP eligibility effective November 1, 2024; bachelor's graduates in these fields no longer qualify for a PGWP
failure_patterns.consequence: PGWP application denial
warning_signs: Program is in general business, liberal arts, or certain social science fields
Program started on or after November 1, 2024

failure_patterns.pattern: H-1B petition filed by IT staffing firm placing worker at third-party client site
failure_patterns.why_it_happens: USCIS identifies third-party placement as the single biggest red flag in H-1B adjudications; body-shop and IT staffing arrangements face the highest scrutiny category
failure_patterns.consequence: Elevated denial rates (approaching 20%) and RFE rates (35%+); denial results in worker losing H-1B status and potentially falling out of authorized work status
warning_signs: Employer business model involves placing workers at client sites rather than internal projects
Employer is categorized as IT staffing or body-shop consulting

failure_patterns.pattern: Graduate submits PGWP application after study permit has already expired
failure_patterns.why_it_happens: Maintained status work authorization during PGWP processing is only available if the application was filed before study permit expiry
failure_patterns.consequence: Loss of authorization to work legally during the approximately 8-month PGWP processing period; potential loss of immigration status
warning_signs: Graduate delays PGWP application by weeks or months after convocation
Study permit expiry date is approaching or has passed at time of application

failure_patterns.pattern: H-1B petition filed at Level I (entry-level) wage
failure_patterns.why_it_happens: USCIS scrutinizes Level I filings as potentially not qualifying as specialty occupations; Level I RFE rate is 34.2% versus 6.8% for Level IV — a 5x difference
failure_patterns.consequence: RFE issued requiring additional evidence that the position qualifies as a specialty occupation; if RFE response is insufficient, petition is denied
warning_signs: Employer offers salary at or near the 17th percentile for the occupation and location
LCA wage level certified at Level I

failure_patterns.pattern: PGWP holder works only in TEER 4 or TEER 5 occupations for the full duration of their PGWP
failure_patterns.why_it_happens: TEER 4 and TEER 5 work is legally permitted under a PGWP but is explicitly excluded from CEC-eligible work experience
failure_patterns.consequence: PGWP holder fails to accumulate the 1 year of skilled (TEER 0-3) Canadian work experience required for Canadian Experience Class eligibility; PGWP expires without achieving permanent residency pathway through CEC
warning_signs: Employment in retail trade, food services, or accommodation throughout PGWP period
No effort to secure TEER 0, 1, 2, or 3 employment

failure_patterns.pattern: Candidate not selected in H-1B lottery despite qualified petition
failure_patterns.why_it_happens: FY2025: 442,000 unique beneficiaries entered for 85,000 available slots (5x oversubscription); selection rate approximately 35.3%; 300,000–350,000 qualified applicants blocked annually due to cap limitations
failure_patterns.consequence: Petition not selected; employer cannot file full H-1B petition; worker cannot obtain H-1B status for that fiscal year and must wait for next lottery cycle or find alternative status
warning_signs: Relying solely on H-1B lottery without backup status plan
Employer only participates in cap-subject lottery and is not cap-exempt

failure_patterns.pattern: Express Entry candidate pays for or relies on LMIA-backed job offer to boost CRS score after Spring 2025
failure_patterns.why_it_happens: Some immigration consultants sold fraudulent or inflated LMIA letters; IRCC removed LMIA arranged employment points from the CRS effective Spring 2025 to address this fraud vector
failure_patterns.consequence: No CRS points awarded for LMIA-backed job offer; financial loss if fees were paid for LMIA; potential fraud exposure if LMIA was purchased
warning_signs: Candidate was advised by consultant to obtain LMIA-backed offer for CRS boost after December 18, 2024 announcement
Candidate is counting on 50 or 200 CRS point uplift from job offer

failure_patterns.pattern: Employer pays H-1B worker below certified LCA prevailing wage
failure_patterns.why_it_happens: DOL prevailing wage requirement mandates employer pay the higher of prevailing wage or actual wage; the LCA wage creates a binding legal floor
failure_patterns.consequence: DOL violation; potential back wages liability; employer debarment from future H-1B filings; adverse effect on worker's status
warning_signs: Employer salary offer falls below DOL OFLC prevailing wage for occupation and location
Employer requests worker accept reduced hours or unpaid periods

failure_patterns.pattern: Working in TEER 4/5 roles for the full PGWP duration without recognizing CEC ineligibility
failure_patterns.why_it_happens: PGWP holders conflate 'legally working in Canada' with 'accumulating PR-eligible experience' — the permit allows work at any level, but CEC requires TEER 0-3; this distinction is not surfaced at the time of employment
failure_patterns.consequence: Graduate reaches end of PGWP with no CEC-eligible experience, facing permit expiry without a clear PR pathway despite years of Canadian employment
warning_signs: Current job is in retail, food service, or accommodation sector
NOC code for current role is TEER 4 or 5 on the IRCC classification table

failure_patterns.pattern: Assuming only large tech companies sponsor H-1B and ignoring mid-sized employers

failure_patterns.consequence: Job seekers over-compete for a small number of high-brand employers while ignoring the majority of the sponsorship market, reducing their odds and limiting their options
