real_case_outcomes.lesson: Headcount rejections are not permanent rejections; maintaining recruiter relationships after a near-miss can convert a timing failure into a deferred offer with no additional interviewing required
real_case_outcomes._source: zhihu_CS专业留学生毕业之后留美的难度有多大.txt

real_case_outcomes.situation: International student, introverted, self-described near-zero networking skills, commerce background, worked at a Chinese company post-graduation, acquired PR via Express Entry
real_case_outcomes.decision: Instead of forcing networking, invested heavily in developing technical skills (Photoshop, Premiere, Final Cut, InDesign) and built a strong portfolio; brought the portfolio to every interview as a concrete demonstration of work quality
real_case_outcomes.outcome: Secured a job at UBC in a competitive multi-round process; interviewer explicitly commented on her portfolio and software test scores being very high
real_case_outcomes.lesson: For introverted candidates who cannot compete on networking, building a demonstrable technical skill set and tangible portfolio can substitute for referral advantage — but requires investment during school years, not after graduation
real_case_outcomes._source: zhihu_加拿大留学生在本地找工作有多难.txt

real_case_outcomes.situation: International CS student who failed H-1B lottery but worked at a major tech company (implicitly Microsoft) during OPT
real_case_outcomes.decision: Leveraged employer's existing Canada transfer program to relocate to Canadian office
real_case_outcomes.outcome: Continued employment without interruption; maintained career trajectory through employer-sponsored Canada pathway
real_case_outcomes.lesson: Large tech companies (Microsoft, Amazon, Google) have established pathways to transfer employees to Canada when H-1B lottery fails; this option should be researched and negotiated before OPT expires, not after
real_case_outcomes._source: zhihu_在美国名校毕业后找工作有多难.txt

real_case_outcomes.situation: Design student searching for a position at a specific company with no publicly posted opening and no known contacts there
real_case_outcomes.decision: Found a company alumni on LinkedIn (the Global Chief Creative Officer), sent a cold connection request and email referencing the shared school connection
real_case_outcomes.outcome: Received an interview invitation from the company's recruiter within two days and ultimately received an offer
real_case_outcomes.lesson: Alumni connections — even to very senior people — can shortcut the formal application process; the shared institutional identity creates enough of a hook to prompt action even from executives
real_case_outcomes._source: zhihu_留学生在美国找工作怎么找.txt

real_case_outcomes.situation: IT graduate (anonymous) who took Costco cashier job (TEER 5) while searching for tech roles; assumed any Canadian work experience counted
real_case_outcomes.decision: Worked Costco cashier for 14 months on PGWP as income source while job searching; did not verify NOC TEER classification
real_case_outcomes.outcome: After 14 months of work experience, discovered TEER 5 hours do not count toward CEC; effectively had zero CEC-eligible hours despite 14 months of Canadian employment; PGWP duration substantially consumed
real_case_outcomes.lesson: TEER level verification before accepting any job is non-negotiable for PR strategy; the TEER 4/5 trap is both common and almost entirely avoidable with basic research
real_case_outcomes._source: canada_job_search_real_experiences.txt

real_case_outcomes.situation: Student secured a LinkedIn internship (FAANG-equivalent prestige) only to find the team culture highly unpleasant — implicit pressure, all-Chinese team dynamic, weekend-boundary violations
real_case_outcomes.decision: Completed the internship while simultaneously interviewing at other companies; declined the return offer and joined a lower-prestige company with better culture fit
real_case_outcomes.outcome: Successfully transitioned to Credit Karma; describes the decision as correct in retrospect and the LinkedIn experience as a useful correction of prestige bias
real_case_outcomes.lesson: Prestige of employer does not predict quality of work experience; team culture varies enormously within large companies and can only be evaluated through direct experience; optimizing for brand at the expense of environment fit is a predictable source of regret
real_case_outcomes._source: zhihu_CS专业留学生毕业之后留美的难度有多大.txt

real_case_outcomes.situation: Commerce student who started working at a bank teller counter in second year of undergraduate study
real_case_outcomes.decision: Continued in banking track, obtained relevant financial certification, moved from teller to advisor role ('sitting in the room' rather than at the counter)
real_case_outcomes.outcome: Became a Financial Service Manager at a BMO branch within one year of graduation
real_case_outcomes.lesson: In banking, starting as a teller during school creates a clear internal promotion pathway to professional roles by graduation — entering from the outside post-graduation is far harder; the internal track is a structural advantage that requires early action
real_case_outcomes._source: zhihu_加拿大留学生在本地找工作有多难.txt

real_case_outcomes.situation: IT professional in Montreal with CRS score of 468; below competitive general draw cut-offs
real_case_outcomes.decision: Invested in Alliance Française French courses + TEF Canada certification over 6 months; achieved French CLB 7+
real_case_outcomes.outcome: CRS score increased from 468 to 516; received ITA in French-language draw at cut-off of 421; described French as 'the single best career investment I made in Canada'
real_case_outcomes.lesson: For candidates with CRS below general draw thresholds, French language investment is a structurally faster PR pathway; Montreal provides immersive environment but the CRS benefit applies nationally
real_case_outcomes._source: canada_job_search_real_experiences.txt

psychological_barriers.trigger: Encountering a 'citizens/PR only' job posting or HR response
psychological_barriers.underlying_state: Injustice sensitivity combined with sunk-cost bias — the candidate has already invested effort in this application and is reluctant to abandon it; awareness of legal protections creates false hope that pushing back will work
psychological_barriers.how_it_manifests: Candidate spends time drafting responses, researching human rights complaints, or attempting to convince HR — all of which yield near-zero job search ROI
psychological_barriers.expert_move: Reframe the question from 'can I fight this?' to 'what is the expected return on this hour of effort vs. applying elsewhere?' — makes the opportunity cost concrete and breaks the sunk-cost loop
psychological_barriers._source: career_canada_PGWP身份找工作全攻略_90投12电话面4技术面2offer.txt

psychological_barriers.trigger: Three consecutive lottery losses with OPT expiring in one month — poster describes searching for a solution only at the final stage
psychological_barriers.underlying_state: Normalization of lottery dependency combined with status-threat anxiety; each lottery cycle feels like a fresh chance, suppressing urgency to build alternatives; when the threat becomes undeniable, panic compresses decision quality
psychological_barriers.how_it_manifests: Candidate does not research or pursue cap-exempt options until forced to by proximity of expiration; the solution existed for three years but was only activated in the final month
psychological_barriers.expert_move: Reframe the first lottery loss as a signal to immediately build a parallel track — not as bad luck requiring patience; introduce cap-exempt employer research as a standard Year 1 OPT task, not a Year 3 emergency measure
psychological_barriers._source: job_search_H_1B_Lottery三连输之后_我最终怎么解决身份问题的.txt

psychological_barriers.trigger: Asking whether to disclose OPT status in the first email (234-like comment asking exactly this)
psychological_barriers.underlying_state: Fear of being caught withholding information; anxiety that non-disclosure will be perceived as deceptive and damage the relationship permanently
psychological_barriers.how_it_manifests: Candidates either disclose too early (triggering automatic rejection) or feel paralyzed about what to say, avoiding cold outreach altogether
psychological_barriers.expert_move: Reframe non-disclosure as sequencing, not deception: 'You are not hiding anything — you are letting them evaluate you as a candidate before a process question becomes a barrier. When asked directly, answer fully and factually.'
psychological_barriers._source: job_search_冷邮件找工作_真实成功案例和模板_OPT身份.txt

psychological_barriers.trigger: Candidate applies to 100-200 large employer postings, receives very few callbacks, and continues applying to the same employer tier while interpreting low response rates as personal failure
psychological_barriers.underlying_state: Sunk cost bias combined with brand anchoring; large employers feel like the 'legitimate' target and abandoning them feels like lowering standards rather than correcting strategy
psychological_barriers.how_it_manifests: Candidate keeps refining resume and cover letter for the same employer tier; asks community 'what am I doing wrong with my resume?' rather than questioning target selection; months pass without pivoting
psychological_barriers.expert_move: Reframe the question from 'why am I not getting callbacks?' to 'is this the right employer pool given current market conditions?'; present data showing that mid-market companies had structurally different callback rates in 2023-2024 and that strategy correction is not a quality concession
psychological_barriers._source: canada_job_search_real_experiences.txt

psychological_barriers.trigger: Student asks 'should I mention my visa status upfront so I don't waste time with companies that won't sponsor?'
psychological_barriers.underlying_state: Rejection anxiety and a desire to regain control by filtering out bad outcomes early; feels like efficiency but is actually avoidance
psychological_barriers.how_it_manifests: Disclosing visa status in cover letters or opening recruiter messages; asking about sponsorship as a first question before any fit assessment
psychological_barriers.expert_move: Reframe: you are not responsible for pre-qualifying employers before they meet you. Your job is to get into the room. The sponsorship conversation happens after they want you — and many employers who 'don't usually sponsor' will for the right candidate
psychological_barriers._source: opt_h1b_job_search_real_experiences.txt

psychological_barriers.trigger: Student asks 'how hard is it to stay in the US with a CS degree?' in a way that seeks validation rather than information
psychological_barriers.underlying_state: Catastrophizing and loss aversion — the student is framing the question to prepare emotionally for failure rather than to identify what actions would change the outcome
psychological_barriers.how_it_manifests: Passive information-seeking on forums rather than active preparation; reading difficulty narratives as confirmation that external factors (visa, discrimination, market) are the binding constraint
psychological_barriers.expert_move: Redirect from the difficulty question to a preparation audit: 'How many problems have you solved? How many companies have you applied to? What does your resume look like?' — converting an emotional question into a diagnostic one
psychological_barriers._source: zhihu_CS专业留学生毕业之后留美的难度有多大.txt

psychological_barriers.trigger: Months of applications with no responses; comparing yourself to peers who found jobs quickly or returned to China for prestigious roles
psychological_barriers.underlying_state: Catastrophizing combined with survivorship bias — the person begins to believe the pattern of rejection reflects a permanent, personal incapacity rather than a structural market challenge with a known timeline
psychological_barriers.how_it_manifests: The first author writes 'I even felt I could not possibly find a good job abroad' and expresses envy toward peers who returned to China; the second author describes 'extreme inner coldness' after 4 months of searching
psychological_barriers.expert_move: Reframe the rejection data as market information, not personal verdict; establish a realistic 6–12 month baseline expectation; introduce parallel income activity (any work) to reduce the psychological weight of the primary search
psychological_barriers._source: zhihu_加拿大留学生在本地找工作有多难.txt

psychological_barriers.trigger: Students describe the job market as 'too hard' or 'impossible' after a small number of rejections (20-50 applications)
psychological_barriers.underlying_state: Attribution error combined with ego protection: it feels less threatening to blame market conditions than to acknowledge insufficient preparation
psychological_barriers.how_it_manifests: Posting on forums about market difficulty, seeking validation that conditions are impossible, stopping the job search prematurely
psychological_barriers.expert_move: Ask the student to report their actual preparation metrics (LeetCode count, application volume, referral attempts) before accepting their market diagnosis; reframe the question from 'is the market hard?' to 'have I met the preparation threshold for my target companies?'
psychological_barriers._source: zhihu_在美国名校毕业后找工作有多难.txt

psychological_barriers.trigger: Sending cold emails without personalizing or researching, then getting no responses
psychological_barriers.underlying_state: Volume-as-safety bias — sending more feels like taking more action and reduces anxiety about passivity, even when quality is what drives outcomes
psychological_barriers.how_it_manifests: Sender reports 'I've sent 50 emails and heard nothing back' while using identical templates with minimal research
psychological_barriers.expert_move: Reframe the goal from 'maximize sends' to 'maximize researched contacts per week' — even 5 well-researched emails beat 50 generic ones; track research depth, not send count
psychological_barriers._source: zhihu_如何进行cold_email.txt

psychological_barriers.trigger: Being deep into a 3-5 month job search with no offers, OPT grace period approaching, and avoiding telling family about the situation
psychological_barriers.underlying_state: Shame-driven isolation — the belief that not having a job is a personal failure that reflects on family investment and cultural expectations, making honest communication feel too costly
psychological_barriers.how_it_manifests: Avoiding calls home, not asking for help, pretending everything is fine while privately breaking down; the poster describes insomnia, full-day paralysis, and crying alone rather than seeking support
psychological_barriers.expert_move: Normalize the timeline — 3-6 months post-graduation is statistically common for international students, not a signal of failure. Reframe family calls as emotional support rather than status reports to reduce the shame loop
psychological_barriers._source: zhihu_留学生在美国找工作怎么找.txt

psychological_barriers.trigger: Students asking 'how do I get H-1B' without first asking 'what is my probability of getting H-1B and what happens if I don't'
psychological_barriers.underlying_state: Optimism bias and status quo anchoring — H-1B is the culturally expected path, so students anchor to it and avoid confronting the statistically likely failure scenario
psychological_barriers.how_it_manifests: Exclusive focus on how to optimize H-1B applications (better employers, better lawyers) rather than building parallel tracks — treating lottery failure as an edge case rather than the base case
psychological_barriers.expert_move: Reframe the question: 'Given that the modal outcome for a Chinese national is lottery failure, what is your plan for that outcome?' Forces concrete contingency planning rather than optimization of a low-probability event
psychological_barriers._source: zhihu_美国留学_留学生如何拿到非盈利机构的H1B_有哪些方法.txt

psychological_barriers.trigger: Comparing a Canadian CAD salary offer to US USD salary numbers
psychological_barriers.underlying_state: Anchoring bias on the nominal number; the currency label is less salient than the magnitude, leading to inflated perception of Canadian compensation
psychological_barriers.how_it_manifests: Candidate feels the Canadian offer is competitive without doing the conversion; may fail to accurately weigh the Canada vs. US decision or feel unexpectedly disappointed after starting
psychological_barriers.expert_move: Build the currency conversion step explicitly into any offer evaluation framework; treat CAD and USD numbers as non-comparable until converted
psychological_barriers._source: career_canada_PGWP身份找工作全攻略_90投12电话面4技术面2offer.txt

psychological_barriers.trigger: Framing cap-exempt roles as a sacrifice or consolation prize due to lower salary
psychological_barriers.underlying_state: Loss aversion and status comparison — the salary reduction feels like a concrete, immediate loss, while the benefit (maintained US work authorization and future earning potential) is abstract and future-oriented
psychological_barriers.how_it_manifests: Candidates reject or delay pursuing cap-exempt options, continuing to wait for a lottery win while OPT time erodes
psychological_barriers.expert_move: Force an expected-value calculation: compare the 1-2 year salary differential against the 10-20 year earning differential between US-based career continuation and departure; commenter [5] made this reframe and it received 189 likes, indicating high resonance
psychological_barriers._source: job_search_H_1B_Lottery三连输之后_我最终怎么解决身份问题的.txt

psychological_barriers.trigger: Receiving a 'we're not hiring right now' reply and abandoning follow-up (156-like comment surfacing this as a stuck point)
psychological_barriers.underlying_state: Rejection sensitivity and learned helplessness; interpreting a situational 'not now' as a permanent 'no' and as confirmation of low prospects
psychological_barriers.how_it_manifests: Candidates stop follow-up with warm contacts entirely, losing relationship capital built through the cold email, and reset to zero with each new outreach
psychological_barriers.expert_move: Acknowledge the signal as timing information, not a rejection: 'Not hiring now' means the relationship has been opened but the timing is wrong — schedule a follow-up in 6–8 weeks and maintain the connection
psychological_barriers._source: job_search_冷邮件找工作_真实成功案例和模板_OPT身份.txt

psychological_barriers.trigger: Candidate hears 'we don't do sponsorship' from an employer and does not respond with a PGWP explanation
psychological_barriers.underlying_state: Internalized shame about immigration status; candidate experiences employer hesitation as rejection rather than confusion, and retreating feels like preserving dignity versus the risk of being turned down explicitly
psychological_barriers.how_it_manifests: Candidate thanks the employer and moves on; frames the outcome as 'they don't hire internationals' in community posts; filters future applications to explicitly sponsorship-open postings
psychological_barriers.expert_move: Destigmatize the correction by framing it as an information asymmetry, not a judgment: 'Most Canadian employers have never heard of PGWP — your job is to be the one who educates them, not to filter yourself out'; provide exact language to use so the conversation feels scripted and low-stakes
psychological_barriers._source: canada_job_search_real_experiences.txt

psychological_barriers.trigger: Student says 'I'll figure out Plan B if I don't get selected in the lottery' when asked about non-selection
psychological_barriers.underlying_state: Optimism bias combined with decision avoidance; the probability of selection (~20–30% in recent years) is treated as a near-certainty because confronting the alternative is emotionally costly
psychological_barriers.how_it_manifests: No concrete Plan B developed before March; student has never researched Canada PGWP pathways, new degree enrollment, or return-home options
psychological_barriers.expert_move: Force the concrete: 'If you find out April 1 that you were not selected, and your OPT expires June 30, what is the first phone call you make?' If they cannot answer this, the Plan B doesn't exist
psychological_barriers._source: opt_h1b_job_search_real_experiences.txt

psychological_barriers.trigger: Student reports that they applied to 20–30 companies with no success and is now considering giving up or returning to China
psychological_barriers.underlying_state: Availability bias — the student has a salient, painful recent experience (rejections) that is cognitively dominating their estimate of the overall probability
psychological_barriers.how_it_manifests: Premature conclusion from an unrepresentative sample; framing of the situation as 'I tried and it didn't work' rather than 'I tried an insufficient amount'
psychological_barriers.expert_move: Provide the base rate: the best answer describes applying to 600+ companies as the high-effort benchmark; reframe 20–30 as not yet a job search, but the beginning of one
psychological_barriers._source: zhihu_CS专业留学生毕业之后留美的难度有多大.txt

psychological_barriers.trigger: Being told by established local Chinese community members that international students 'will never make it and will only wash dishes'
psychological_barriers.underlying_state: Internalized narrative of structural impossibility — absorbing a pessimistic social script from people who may have failed or given up themselves
psychological_barriers.how_it_manifests: The first author explicitly recalls this comment and how it produced 'angry dissatisfaction'; the risk is that some job seekers absorb rather than reject this narrative and lower their ambitions prematurely
psychological_barriers.expert_move: Recognize that negative community narratives often reflect the experience of people who did not use optimal strategies; treat them as warnings about what happens without preparation, not as predictions about what must happen
psychological_barriers._source: zhihu_加拿大留学生在本地找工作有多难.txt

psychological_barriers.trigger: International students in non-CS fields express confusion about why they can't find US employment despite strong academic credentials
psychological_barriers.underlying_state: Credential transferability illusion: students assume the academic prestige and hard work that earned their degree will translate directly into employment value in a market that operates by different rules
psychological_barriers.how_it_manifests: Focusing on GPA and academic reputation while neglecting the structural reality that their field does not have H-1B sponsorship demand
psychological_barriers.expert_move: Separate the academic value of the degree from the employment market reality; introduce the concept of employer sponsorship demand as a variable entirely independent of academic quality
psychological_barriers._source: zhihu_在美国名校毕业后找工作有多难.txt

psychological_barriers.trigger: Opening networking conversations with a long self-introduction and list of accomplishments
psychological_barriers.underlying_state: Fear of being overlooked or underestimated — especially common among international students who feel their credentials need to compensate for perceived disadvantages
psychological_barriers.how_it_manifests: Email or first message is a dense paragraph of credentials, GPA, internships, and skills with no question or invitation for the recipient
psychological_barriers.expert_move: Point out that self-promotion in an opening message signals insecurity, not strength — experienced networkers lead with curiosity about the other person, which paradoxically signals more confidence
psychological_barriers._source: zhihu_如何进行cold_email.txt

psychological_barriers.trigger: Having a coffee chat go well and then waiting passively for the contact to follow up with referral or opportunities
psychological_barriers.underlying_state: Avoidance of rejection — following up feels presumptuous or needy, so students wait passively rather than risk being told no explicitly
psychological_barriers.how_it_manifests: Students do not send follow-up emails, do not ask directly for referrals, and interpret silence as the contact being 'busy' rather than recognizing they need to maintain the relationship actively
psychological_barriers.expert_move: Reframe follow-up as professional courtesy, not as asking for a favor — a thank-you email the next day is expected etiquette, not an imposition. Normalize that contacts are busy and that a prompt, specific follow-up is what keeps you visible
psychological_barriers._source: zhihu_留学生在美国找工作怎么找.txt

psychological_barriers.trigger: Students who have already committed to a Cap-Subject employer asking about alternatives only after receiving lottery rejection
psychological_barriers.underlying_state: Sunk cost fallacy combined with temporal discounting — the relationship with the employer feels too invested to reconsider, and Cap-Exempt alternatives seemed less attractive before the rejection
psychological_barriers.how_it_manifests: Seeking ways to retroactively fix a structurally weak visa position rather than having made Cap-Exempt targeting a selection criterion during job search
psychological_barriers.expert_move: Acknowledge the sunk cost directly: 'The employer relationship is valuable, but the question now is what options exist — can this employer transfer you to a Cap-Exempt affiliate, or does a different employer offer the stability you need?'
psychological_barriers._source: zhihu_美国留学_留学生如何拿到非盈利机构的H1B_有哪些方法.txt

psychological_barriers.trigger: Two months of failed mass applications before trying cold outreach
psychological_barriers.underlying_state: Default bias toward conventional methods combined with sunk cost thinking; the candidate continues a failing strategy because switching feels like admitting the previous effort was wasted
psychological_barriers.how_it_manifests: Continuing to mass apply on Easy Apply despite near-zero conversion, framing it as 'building volume' rather than recognizing it as a failing strategy
psychological_barriers.expert_move: Surface the conversion data explicitly: '200 applications, 3 calls — that is a 1.5% rate. At what point does the evidence tell you this channel is not working for your situation?'
psychological_barriers._source: job_search_冷邮件找工作_真实成功案例和模板_OPT身份.txt

psychological_barriers.trigger: Graduate takes a TEER 4-5 job as 'temporary' income and continues describing it as temporary for months while not actively searching
psychological_barriers.underlying_state: Temporal discounting and cognitive dissonance; labeling the job as temporary reduces the psychological urgency to change it; the label also functions as identity protection — 'I'm not really a cashier, I'm a software engineer between roles'
psychological_barriers.how_it_manifests: Months pass without targeted TEER 0-3 job search activity; candidate continues framing situation as temporary in community posts while CEC clock doesn't run; becomes aware of problem only when approaching PGWP expiry
psychological_barriers.expert_move: Make the opportunity cost concrete and time-specific: 'Every month in a TEER 5 job is one month added to your PR timeline — if you work TEER 5 for 12 months, your ITA date moves 12 months later. What is 12 months of your life in Canada worth to you?'
psychological_barriers._source: canada_job_search_real_experiences.txt

psychological_barriers.trigger: Student stops applying after receiving a verbal sponsorship promise from a startup or small employer
psychological_barriers.underlying_state: Sunk cost and relief — the emotional exhaustion of job searching makes any positive signal feel like a resolution; continuing to apply after a 'yes' feels like betrayal of the relationship
psychological_barriers.how_it_manifests: Student accepts verbal promise as sufficient confirmation; cancels other interviews; waits for formal offer that never comes or comes without H-1B commitment
psychological_barriers.expert_move: Normalize continued searching: 'A verbal promise is a conversation, not a commitment. You're not betraying anyone by keeping your options open until you have a written offer with explicit H-1B language. Professional relationships survive this.'
psychological_barriers._source: opt_h1b_job_search_real_experiences.txt

psychological_barriers.trigger: Student expresses shame about considering a paid prep service (bootcamp or ICC) after failing to find a job independently
psychological_barriers.underlying_state: Identity threat — the student perceives needing external help as evidence of personal inadequacy rather than as a rational resource allocation decision
psychological_barriers.how_it_manifests: Delayed decision to seek help until too late in the OPT window; continuing to attempt independent preparation that has already demonstrated insufficient results
psychological_barriers.expert_move: Normalize paid prep explicitly: 'There's nothing shameful about it' (直接原文: '没啥可耻的'); frame it as a return-on-investment calculation — the cost of a prep program is recoverable in weeks of US tech salary, while the cost of returning to China without a job is not
psychological_barriers._source: zhihu_CS专业留学生毕业之后留美的难度有多大.txt

psychological_barriers.trigger: Feeling that your English is not good enough and will never be good enough compared to native speakers
psychological_barriers.underlying_state: Fixed mindset about language ability combined with performance anxiety — treating a skill gap as an identity rather than a trainable competency
psychological_barriers.how_it_manifests: The first author describes knowing the right words but freezing and only producing 'I'm very good at this...' under interview pressure; the third author notes that non-confidence in English 'will definitely show and be detected by interviewers'
psychological_barriers.expert_move: Reframe English fluency as a performance skill that improves with each interview attempt; use written preparation (scripted answers) to compensate for in-the-moment fluency limits; treat early interview failures as training data rather than validation of the fear
psychological_barriers._source: zhihu_加拿大留学生在本地找工作有多难.txt

psychological_barriers.trigger: Students delay applying to domestic (home country) jobs while pursuing US opportunities, treating domestic employment as an always-available fallback
psychological_barriers.underlying_state: Sunk cost fallacy + optimism bias: having invested heavily in US education, students resist closing the door on US employment and overestimate their ability to activate domestic options on demand
psychological_barriers.how_it_manifests: Missing domestic recruiting windows; arriving at end of OPT with no offer from either market; experiencing shock that domestic fallback is not available
psychological_barriers.expert_move: Reframe dual-track job searching as risk management, not hedging or giving up on US aspirations; treat domestic application deadlines as hard constraints to be tracked in parallel, not sequential fallbacks
psychological_barriers._source: zhihu_在美国名校毕业后找工作有多难.txt

psychological_barriers.trigger: Receiving consecutive rejections or no responses after a large application batch
psychological_barriers.underlying_state: Sunk cost and learned helplessness — the energy already invested in applications makes stopping or changing strategy feel like wasting prior effort; repeated rejection creates a generalized sense that the system is fixed against you
psychological_barriers.how_it_manifests: Continuing to apply in the same way at the same volume rather than diagnosing the conversion problem; refusing to seek resume or interview feedback because it might confirm the fear of being unqualified
psychological_barriers.expert_move: Reframe job search as a measurement problem, not a judgment problem — low conversion rate is diagnostic data, not a verdict. Introduce a structured review of where in the funnel candidates are dropping (no response = resume problem; no offer after interviews = interview problem)
psychological_barriers._source: zhihu_留学生在美国找工作怎么找.txt

psychological_barriers.trigger: Regulated profession graduate says 'I'll start the licensing process once I get my work permit' and waits passively for PGWP
psychological_barriers.underlying_state: Sequential planning bias; humans default to linear task ordering even when parallel processing is both possible and clearly superior; the logic 'I need work authorization before I can work, so I need the permit first' feels correct even when it isn't
psychological_barriers.how_it_manifests: Candidate correctly files PGWP on graduation day but makes no contact with CNO/PEO; 8 months pass; PGWP arrives and licensing process begins from zero; total timeline to employment in field extends to 14-20 months
psychological_barriers.expert_move: Explicitly surface the false assumption: 'Licensing bodies do not require you to have your work permit before they process your application — they are independent processes. The question is not which to do first, it is how to do both at the same time.'
psychological_barriers._source: canada_job_search_real_experiences.txt

psychological_barriers.trigger: Student asks whether to apply to a startup with good culture fit despite its lack of H-1B history, describing it as a 'tough decision'
psychological_barriers.underlying_state: Cultural fit and excitement about the role create motivated reasoning to overlook structural red flags; the desire for a specific outcome distorts risk assessment
psychological_barriers.how_it_manifests: Student seeks community validation to apply anyway; frames H-1B history absence as a minor concern rather than a near-disqualifier
psychological_barriers.expert_move: Separate the job decision from the visa decision: 'Would you take this job if it required you to leave the US in 12 months with no path to stay? Because that's what 70% of startup sponsorship promises lead to. If yes, great — go in clear-eyed. If no, that's your answer.'
psychological_barriers._source: opt_h1b_job_search_real_experiences.txt

psychological_barriers.trigger: Student describes working at a prestigious company (FAANG) as a goal they pursued for years, then discovers the reality is disappointing
psychological_barriers.underlying_state: Idealization and surrogate goal substitution — the student conflated 'working at Google/LinkedIn' (an observable, socially validated milestone) with 'having a good work life' (the actual goal)
psychological_barriers.how_it_manifests: Shock and demoralization upon experiencing the gap between company brand and actual team environment; difficulty making the rational decision to leave because of sunk cost in the goal pursuit
psychological_barriers.expert_move: Reframe prestige as a means, not an end: the informed pattern is to use large-company experience as a resume credential while actively evaluating whether the specific team is a good fit, and to leave without guilt when it is not
psychological_barriers._source: zhihu_CS专业留学生毕业之后留美的难度有多大.txt

psychological_barriers.trigger: Identifying as introverted and using it to explain and justify avoiding all networking
psychological_barriers.underlying_state: Identity-based avoidance — framing a situational discomfort as a fixed personality trait to avoid the anxiety of rejection in networking contexts
psychological_barriers.how_it_manifests: Both the first and third authors explicitly describe themselves as introverted with 'negative networking skills'; the first author treats this as a complete excuse to skip networking entirely, only partially compensating with technical skill development
psychological_barriers.expert_move: Separate introversion (a preference) from networking incapacity (a skill); offer a lower-stakes entry point — LinkedIn messaging requires no real-time performance; even one informational chat per week compounds significantly over a 6-month search
psychological_barriers._source: zhihu_加拿大留学生在本地找工作有多难.txt

psychological_barriers.trigger: Students express paralysis about whether to 'waste time' on LeetCode preparation versus school coursework
psychological_barriers.underlying_state: Identity conflict: students who self-identify as 'good students' resist deprioritizing academic performance, even when the evidence suggests coursework has near-zero job market return
psychological_barriers.how_it_manifests: Over-investing in coursework, selecting hard courses to maintain identity as high-achiever, then entering recruiting season under-prepared for technical interviews
psychological_barriers.expert_move: Validate the academic identity while reframing what 'preparation' means in this context: 'You're not slacking — you're optimizing for the actual exam, which is the technical interview, not your GPA'
psychological_barriers._source: zhihu_在美国名校毕业后找工作有多难.txt

psychological_barriers.trigger: Feeling too introverted or anxious to attend networking events, choosing to apply online instead
psychological_barriers.underlying_state: Social anxiety combined with a cognitive distortion that online applications are an equivalent substitute for in-person relationship-building
psychological_barriers.how_it_manifests: Students rationalize staying home as 'applying more efficiently' when the actual driver is avoidance of social discomfort; the poster names this pattern directly ('I want to stay home, watch Netflix, why do I have to meet people I don't know')
psychological_barriers.expert_move: Acknowledge the discomfort is real while clarifying that the discomfort is the cost of entry, not a signal to avoid the activity — and that each event gets easier with practice. Suggest low-stakes starting points (small alumni dinners, virtual events) before large career fairs
psychological_barriers._source: zhihu_留学生在美国找工作怎么找.txt

psychological_barriers.trigger: Candidate with CRS below competitive draw thresholds focuses exclusively on job search and dismisses French language investment as 'not relevant to me'
psychological_barriers.underlying_state: Identity foreclosure and effort aversion; learning French feels like a fundamental identity change rather than a strategic tool; the effort required (6+ months of study) triggers avoidance framing
psychological_barriers.how_it_manifests: Candidate continues monitoring Express Entry draws hoping cut-offs will drop; deprioritizes French indefinitely; does not calculate actual CRS uplift or compare French-language draw cut-offs to their score
psychological_barriers.expert_move: Reframe French as a financial instrument rather than a cultural identity: 'French CLB 7+ is worth approximately 80-100 CRS points. What would it cost you in time and money to get 80 CRS points any other way? Calculate the ROI before dismissing it.'
psychological_barriers._source: canada_job_search_real_experiences.txt

psychological_barriers.trigger: Student frames their situation as 'I have a year on OPT so I have time to be selective'
psychological_barriers.underlying_state: Availability bias — the 12-month OPT authorization feels like 12 months of runway, when the effective window is the 90-day unemployment cap minus days already consumed
psychological_barriers.how_it_manifests: Student takes a post-graduation summer break; begins serious applications in September when the unemployment clock has already consumed 3+ months
psychological_barriers.expert_move: Make the clock visible: 'Your OPT isn't 12 months of job searching. It's 90 days of unemployment. Pull up your EAD and count from day one. How many days have you already used?'
psychological_barriers._source: opt_h1b_job_search_real_experiences.txt

psychological_barriers.trigger: Student from a non-CS background (EE, chemistry) asks whether it is too late to transition into CS
psychological_barriers.underlying_state: Temporal anxiety and comparison paralysis — the student is measuring their current state against CS-native peers and interpreting the gap as permanent rather than as a preparation problem
psychological_barriers.how_it_manifests: Asking permission-seeking questions ('can I still make it?') rather than action-oriented ones ('what do I need to do?')
psychological_barriers.expert_move: Provide a concrete, unconditional answer (Answer [1] FAQ section: 'You can, as long as you want it and are willing to do the work') paired with a specific first action — start LeetCode, revise the resume to remove irrelevant content, find one CS project to add
psychological_barriers._source: zhihu_CS专业留学生毕业之后留美的难度有多大.txt

psychological_barriers.trigger: Receiving a job offer from a low-quality Chinese-owned company when desperate and anxious
psychological_barriers.underlying_state: Relief-seeking behavior driven by anxiety — the immediate reduction in uncertainty from receiving any offer overrides rational evaluation of whether the offer actually serves long-term goals
psychological_barriers.how_it_manifests: The first author acknowledges accepting the Chinese company offer explicitly because of immigration urgency despite knowing the reputation — 'I had no choice'; the danger is this becoming a 2–3 year trap
psychological_barriers.expert_move: Before accepting, define the specific exit criteria (e.g., immigration application filed, X months of experience gained) and set a hard date; do not let relief at having an offer become passive acceptance of the situation indefinitely
psychological_barriers._source: zhihu_加拿大留学生在本地找工作有多难.txt

reframing_moves.original_framing: How do I deal with employers who are worried about my visa status as a PGWP holder?
reframing_moves.reframe: Your job is to eliminate the employer's assumption of complexity before they form it — not to overcome objections after they arise
reframing_moves.why_it_works: Shifts the candidate from a reactive posture (defending their status) to a proactive one (preemptively removing friction); changes the mental model from 'visa problem to explain' to 'administrative simplicity to communicate'
reframing_moves.example_language: 「您完全不需要为我申请任何东西，我可以直接入职工作。」(You don't need to do anything for me — I can start work directly.)
reframing_moves._source: career_canada_PGWP身份找工作全攻略_90投12电话面4技术面2offer.txt

reframing_moves.original_framing: The cap-exempt job pays 30% less — is it really worth it?
reframing_moves.reframe: Compare the salary reduction not to your current salary, but to the opportunity cost of being forced out of the US entirely — the expected value of maintaining US status dwarfs a temporary pay cut
reframing_moves.why_it_works: Shifts the comparison from a local loss (salary vs. salary) to a global expected value calculation (US career trajectory vs. departure), making the decision mathematically obvious rather than emotionally difficult
reframing_moves.example_language: 尤其是和被迫回国或者转去加拿大的机会成本比较的话 (especially when compared to the opportunity cost of being forced to return home or move to Canada)
reframing_moves._source: job_search_H_1B_Lottery三连输之后_我最终怎么解决身份问题的.txt

reframing_moves.original_framing: I need to find a job — how do I apply to as many places as possible?
reframing_moves.reframe: You do not have an application volume problem; you have a targeting and entry-point problem. The question is not how many companies you reach, but whether you are reaching the right person at the right moment through the right channel.
reframing_moves.why_it_works: Shifts focus from effort quantity (applications sent) to strategy quality (conversion rate and channel selection), which is the actual lever for OPT candidates who face structural filtering in standard channels
reframing_moves.example_language: The post's own data makes the reframe concrete: 40 targeted emails beat 200 mass applications by 10x on interview rate
reframing_moves._source: job_search_冷邮件找工作_真实成功案例和模板_OPT身份.txt

reframing_moves.original_framing: 'The employer said they don't do sponsorship, so they won't hire me'
reframing_moves.reframe: The employer doesn't know what a PGWP is — this is an information problem, not a rejection
reframing_moves.why_it_works: Converts a perceived closed door into an open conversation; shifts the candidate's posture from resignation to action; aligns with the structural reality that employer confusion is the most common barrier, not hostility
reframing_moves.example_language: "Most employers say 'we don't sponsor' because they've heard about H-1B. If you explain 'I have an open work permit, you don't do anything,' most of them immediately say 'oh, that's totally fine.'"
reframing_moves._source: canada_job_search_real_experiences.txt

reframing_moves.original_framing: I'm trying to figure out which companies will sponsor me before I apply, so I don't waste time
reframing_moves.reframe: You're not filtering employers — you're filtering yourself out. Verify H-1B history via H1BData.info, then apply and let the process surface the real answer
reframing_moves.why_it_works: Shifts the student from a defensive stance (pre-filtering to avoid rejection) to an offensive stance (targeted application with verification); separates legitimate due diligence (H-1B history check) from counterproductive self-filtering (asking about sponsorship before interviews)
reframing_moves.example_language: Check their petition history, not their willingness — willingness you earn in the interview, history you can verify in two minutes
reframing_moves._source: opt_h1b_job_search_real_experiences.txt

reframing_moves.original_framing: 'How hard is it for CS international students to stay in the US after graduation?' — framed as a fixed external difficulty question
reframing_moves.reframe: The best answer reframes it as: 'The difficulty level is almost entirely determined by your preparation level — the people saying it's hard are overwhelmingly the people who didn't prepare'
reframing_moves.why_it_works: Converts a passive assessment of external conditions into an actionable internal audit; shifts locus of control from market/visa to preparation behavior
reframing_moves.example_language: 如果一个人CS背景+简历+刷题+投公司，每个都做了，说实话我没见过留不下来的 (If someone has done all four — CS background, resume, LeetCode, applications — honestly I've never seen anyone who couldn't stay)
reframing_moves._source: zhihu_CS专业留学生毕业之后留美的难度有多大.txt

reframing_moves.original_framing: I'm an introvert so I can't network — I just have to accept that I'll be disadvantaged
reframing_moves.reframe: Since you can't compete on networking, invest that energy into building technical skills and a tangible portfolio that does the talking for you in interviews
reframing_moves.why_it_works: It shifts from a fixed deficit narrative to an actionable alternative strategy; it accepts the constraint rather than fighting it, and redirects energy productively
reframing_moves.example_language: 'If you think you are the introverted type, consider expanding your technical skills instead — my PPT score was noted as very very high by my future boss'
reframing_moves._source: zhihu_加拿大留学生在本地找工作有多难.txt

reframing_moves.original_framing: CS job search in the US is very hard / the market is terrible
reframing_moves.reframe: The question is not whether the market is hard — it's whether you have met the preparation threshold. Most people complaining about difficulty online have solved under 200 problems and applied to under 50 companies. CS is still the best-positioned field for international students by a wide margin.
reframing_moves.why_it_works: Shifts focus from an external, uncontrollable variable (market conditions) to internal, controllable variables (preparation depth, application volume); breaks the helplessness framing
reframing_moves.example_language: 'CS找工作再难，也是全美第一的最好找工作的专业，没有之一。说找工作难的，90%都是这样的人在这说，自己没怎么努力。'
reframing_moves._source: zhihu_在美国名校毕业后找工作有多难.txt

reframing_moves.original_framing: How do I write a cold email that gets me a referral or job lead?
reframing_moves.reframe: Networking is about meeting new people — the referral is a possible byproduct, not the goal
reframing_moves.why_it_works: Shifts the sender's internal orientation from extraction to connection, which changes the tone of every sentence in the email and makes it more likely to generate a genuine response
reframing_moves.example_language: 归根结底，networking的本质就是：认识新的朋友 (The essence of networking is simply: meeting new people)
reframing_moves._source: zhihu_如何进行cold_email.txt

reframing_moves.original_framing: I need to network more — I should go to more events and have more coffee chats to find a job
reframing_moves.reframe: Networking is not about volume of contacts — it's about whether you can give someone a specific, concrete reason to stake their reputation on you. Ask yourself: why would a person who met you 30 minutes ago fill out a referral form for you?
reframing_moves.why_it_works: Shifts focus from activity (attending events) to outcome (building a credible case for referral), which forces candidates to honestly assess whether they have a compelling enough value proposition before expecting referrals
reframing_moves.example_language: Refer别人很烦的，要填一堆表格… 你真的有那么好值得refer嘛
reframing_moves._source: zhihu_留学生在美国找工作怎么找.txt

reframing_moves.original_framing: 'How do I get a nonprofit H-1B?' — treating Cap-Exempt H-1B as a special trick or hack to game the system
reframing_moves.reframe: Cap-Exempt H-1B is not a loophole — it reflects a structural difference in employer type. The real question is whether your career goals are compatible with working at universities, nonprofit research organizations, or affiliated nonprofits, because that's the actual requirement
reframing_moves.why_it_works: Shifts the student from looking for a shortcut to evaluating genuine employer fit, which is a more stable and actionable frame — it connects visa strategy to job search targeting rather than treating them as separate problems
reframing_moves.example_language: The question isn't how to get Cap-Exempt H-1B — the question is whether you're willing to target employers that qualify for it
reframing_moves._source: zhihu_美国留学_留学生如何拿到非盈利机构的H1B_有哪些方法.txt

reframing_moves.original_framing: I chose Canada for the immigration pathway — how does it compare to the US in terms of career outcome?
reframing_moves.reframe: Canada's value proposition is immigration certainty, not compensation; evaluate the two countries on different dimensions rather than treating them as equivalent alternatives
reframing_moves.why_it_works: Prevents the false equivalence of comparing raw salary numbers across currencies; helps candidates make the decision with accurate expectations rather than discovering the gap post-arrival
reframing_moves.example_language: 「选择加拿大主要是移民路径确定性，不是薪资。」(The reason to choose Canada is immigration pathway certainty, not salary.)
reframing_moves._source: career_canada_PGWP身份找工作全攻略_90投12电话面4技术面2offer.txt

reframing_moves.original_framing: I've lost the lottery three times — I'm running out of options
reframing_moves.reframe: You haven't lost access to H-1B — you've only lost access to cap-subject H-1B; cap-exempt H-1B is a different track with no lottery that was available to you the entire time
reframing_moves.why_it_works: Dissolves the perceived finality of lottery losses by revealing a structurally different pathway that was never closed; replaces scarcity framing with option-expansion framing
reframing_moves.example_language: 大学附属的研究院是H-1B cap-exempt的，不用抽签，可以全年随时申请 (university-affiliated research institutes are H-1B cap-exempt, no lottery required, can be filed any time of year)
reframing_moves._source: job_search_H_1B_Lottery三连输之后_我最终怎么解决身份问题的.txt

reframing_moves.original_framing: Should I disclose my OPT status upfront to avoid wasting time?
reframing_moves.reframe: The question is not whether to disclose — you must be honest when asked. The question is sequencing: establish that you are a strong candidate before the conversation gets to process-level questions about visa.
reframing_moves.why_it_works: Separates honesty (non-negotiable) from sequencing (strategic), dissolving the false choice between 'hide it' and 'lead with it' — both of which are suboptimal
reframing_moves.example_language: '先让对方对你这个人感兴趣' — let them get interested in you as a person first
reframing_moves._source: job_search_冷邮件找工作_真实成功案例和模板_OPT身份.txt

reframing_moves.original_framing: 'I'm working a temporary job at Costco while I search — I just need to keep looking until I find a tech role'
reframing_moves.reframe: The TEER level of your current job is not a lifestyle question — it is a PR timeline question; TEER 5 hours do not count, so every month in this role is a month added to your PR timeline
reframing_moves.why_it_works: Converts an abstract 'suboptimal situation' into a concrete, quantifiable cost; replaces the comfortable label of 'temporary' with a specific opportunity cost that creates urgency
reframing_moves.example_language: "It doesn't matter that it's temporary — what matters is that TEER 5 doesn't count for CEC. You can be 'temporarily' working Costco for 18 months and still be at zero CEC hours. That's 18 months of PR delay."
reframing_moves._source: canada_job_search_real_experiences.txt

reframing_moves.original_framing: I'm waiting to see if I get selected in the lottery before I think about what to do next
reframing_moves.reframe: The lottery is not a decision — it's an event. Your decisions happen before and after it. What have you already decided to do if you're not selected?
reframing_moves.why_it_works: Breaks the passivity loop by separating the uncontrollable event (lottery outcome) from the controllable decision (Plan B preparation); forces concrete planning rather than suspended waiting
reframing_moves.example_language: By December, you should be able to answer 'what happens if I'm not selected' in one sentence with a real plan, not a shrug
reframing_moves._source: opt_h1b_job_search_real_experiences.txt

reframing_moves.original_framing: 'I applied to companies and got rejected — the job market is too difficult for international students'
reframing_moves.reframe: The best answer reframes it as: 'You haven't applied enough to have a valid data point — 20 applications is not a job search for an international student, it's a warm-up'
reframing_moves.why_it_works: Removes the false sense of having genuinely tried by replacing it with a concrete, quantified benchmark (200+ applications); prevents premature attribution of failure to external causes
reframing_moves.example_language: 北美投简历，少于200家都是没努力 (In North America, applying to fewer than 200 companies means you haven't tried)
reframing_moves._source: zhihu_CS专业留学生毕业之后留美的难度有多大.txt

reframing_moves.original_framing: I only have 30 seconds to a minute of things to say in an interview while native speakers go for 2–3 minutes — I just can't compete
reframing_moves.reframe: Compensate for speaking time with visual evidence — bring your portfolio and let your past work outputs speak instead of relying on verbal fluency alone
reframing_moves.why_it_works: It converts a verbal disadvantage into a visual advantage; most native speakers do not bring portfolios, so this creates a differentiating signal rather than a leveling one
reframing_moves.example_language: 'I can't match their 2–3 minutes? Fine. I brought my portfolio to show them my past work. Turns out that worked.'
reframing_moves._source: zhihu_加拿大留学生在本地找工作有多难.txt

reframing_moves.original_framing: I've applied to 20-30 companies and haven't gotten any interviews — is the market really this bad?
reframing_moves.reframe: 20-30 applications is not a sufficient sample size to diagnose market conditions for an international candidate. The baseline for meaningful signal is 200+ applications; anything below that is a measurement of effort, not market receptivity.
reframing_moves.why_it_works: Replaces a market diagnosis (which produces helplessness) with an effort diagnosis (which produces a clear action: apply more); contextualizes the international student's situation against domestic baselines
reframing_moves.example_language: '北美投简历，少于200家都是没努力。我们在北美是外国人，你20家努力了？'
reframing_moves._source: zhihu_在美国名校毕业后找工作有多难.txt

reframing_moves.original_framing: I can't find a job — the market is bad / companies don't want to sponsor / I'm not good enough
reframing_moves.reframe: Job search is a numbers game with a known conversion ratio. If you've sent 200 applications and have 1 offer, that's 0.5% — which is actually a data point, not a verdict on your worth. The question is: where is the funnel breaking down?
reframing_moves.why_it_works: Converts a shame narrative ('I'm not good enough') into a diagnostic problem ('where in the process am I losing people'), which is actionable and emotionally less paralyzing
reframing_moves.example_language: 找工作是个numbers game，意思是你投大概15封简历能有一个面试，投100封简历，说不定能有一个offer
reframing_moves._source: zhihu_留学生在美国找工作怎么找.txt

reframing_moves.original_framing: 'Only 10% of Chinese students successfully stay in the US' framed as a discouraging statistic
reframing_moves.reframe: That 10% figure tells you what happens when students use the default strategy — it doesn't tell you the success rate for students who proactively targeted Cap-Exempt employers, built O-1A evidence, or had STEM OPT runway for multiple lottery attempts
reframing_moves.why_it_works: Converts a paralyzing aggregate statistic into a conditional probability question — the 10% is the baseline for reactive students, not for students who differentiate their strategy
reframing_moves.example_language: The 10% is what happens on autopilot. The question is what the rate is for people who chose their employer specifically for Cap-Exempt status
reframing_moves._source: zhihu_美国留学_留学生如何拿到非盈利机构的H1B_有哪些方法.txt

reframing_moves.original_framing: 'I have a low CRS score — I just need to wait for a lower cut-off draw or get a job offer'
reframing_moves.reframe: French language is a lever that can add the equivalent of 80-100 CRS points in 6 months — have you calculated whether that investment beats waiting?
reframing_moves.why_it_works: Introduces a quantifiable alternative that the poster may not have considered; replaces passive waiting with an active investment decision; reframes French as a financial/strategic tool rather than a cultural identity requirement
reframing_moves.example_language: "French CLB 7 is worth more CRS points than most people realize. French-language draw cut-offs have been running 60-100 points lower than general draws. Have you calculated your score with French? Because if it puts you in range of those draws, 6 months of French study might be faster than 2 years of waiting."
reframing_moves._source: canada_job_search_real_experiences.txt

reframing_moves.original_framing: My OPT gives me a year to find a job, so I can be selective and take my time
reframing_moves.reframe: Your OPT gives you 90 days of unemployment, not a year of searching. The year is how long you can work — not how long you can look
reframing_moves.why_it_works: Corrects a fundamental misunderstanding about the structure of OPT authorization; transforms urgency from abstract to concrete by anchoring on the actual constraint (90 days) rather than the perceived constraint (12 months)
reframing_moves.example_language: Pull up your EAD. Count the days since it started. That's how much unemployment time you've used. How many do you have left?
reframing_moves._source: opt_h1b_job_search_real_experiences.txt

reframing_moves.original_framing: 'Should I focus on my coursework and GPA, or on finding a job?'
reframing_moves.reframe: The best answer reframes it as a false tradeoff with a clear answer: 'Nobody will ever ask your GPA; everyone will ask where you work — this is not a difficult optimization'
reframing_moves.why_it_works: Collapses what feels like a genuine dilemma into a decision with a dominant option; removes the cognitive burden of balance-seeking by making the asymmetry of payoffs explicit
reframing_moves.example_language: 毕业了没人问你GPA多少，都会问你去哪工作了，所以分清孰轻孰重 (After graduation no one asks your GPA, everyone asks where you work — understand what matters more)
reframing_moves._source: zhihu_CS专业留学生毕业之后留美的难度有多大.txt

reframing_moves.original_framing: My English isn't good enough — I freeze in interviews and can't express how capable I am
reframing_moves.reframe: Treat interview English as a performance skill you can systematically prepare for, not a fixed ability — write out and rehearse 100 interview answers until fluency under pressure becomes procedural
reframing_moves.why_it_works: It moves from a capability attribution ('my English is bad') to a preparation attribution ('I haven't practiced enough') — the latter is actionable, the former is paralyzing
reframing_moves.example_language: 'I prepared answers to 100 common interview questions and practiced them walking in the park. Let's see what new questions you can ask me.'
reframing_moves._source: zhihu_加拿大留学生在本地找工作有多难.txt

reframing_moves.original_framing: Should I focus on getting good grades or finding a job?
reframing_moves.reframe: GPA is not the gatekeeping variable for employment. The gatekeepers are LeetCode performance, project quality, and internship experience. Once you understand what the actual 'exam' is, the resource allocation question answers itself.
reframing_moves.why_it_works: Removes the false trade-off framing by identifying which metric actually matters; students can deprioritize coursework without feeling like they're failing — they're just redirecting effort toward the correct evaluation criteria
reframing_moves.example_language: '毕业了没人问你GPA多少，都会问你去哪工作了，所以分清孰轻孰重。'
reframing_moves._source: zhihu_在美国名校毕业后找工作有多难.txt

reframing_moves.original_framing: No one is helping me — my professor stopped replying, my contacts are ghosting me
reframing_moves.reframe: No one has an obligation to help you. People are busy and you are not their priority. The only reliable variable in your job search is your own effort. Build a system that doesn't depend on any single person following through.
reframing_moves.why_it_works: Removes the victim frame and the dependency on others, replacing it with a self-reliance frame that is both psychologically empowering and practically correct — parallel pipelines are more robust than single-thread relationships
reframing_moves.example_language: 没有人有义务帮你，所以虽然相信人性是好的，但是要知道大家都很忙，no one gives a fuck。靠自己，最靠谱
reframing_moves._source: zhihu_留学生在美国找工作怎么找.txt

reframing_moves.original_framing: 'I'm applying to Shopify, Amazon, RBC — but I'm not getting callbacks. What's wrong with my resume?'
reframing_moves.reframe: The problem may not be your resume — it may be your target pool; large employers in Canada were structurally flooded in 2023-2024 and the same candidate would get callbacks at mid-market companies
reframing_moves.why_it_works: Decouples self-worth from callback rate; converts what feels like a personal failure into a market structure problem with a concrete strategic fix; removes the false premise that more polish on the same strategy will produce different results
reframing_moves.example_language: "You could have a perfect resume and still not get callbacks from Shopify in 2024 — they had thousands of applications. The question is not 'why am I failing?' but 'am I in the right pool?' A 175-person fintech in Waterloo gets 10 applications for the same role."
reframing_moves._source: canada_job_search_real_experiences.txt

reframing_moves.original_framing: The startup said they'll sponsor me — should I stop applying to other places?
reframing_moves.reframe: A sponsorship conversation is not a sponsorship commitment. You haven't received an offer yet, let alone a written H-1B intent. You're not in a relationship with them — you're in a process
reframing_moves.why_it_works: Names the emotional confusion between social commitment (feeling obligated to reciprocate the startup's enthusiasm) and legal/professional reality (nothing is binding without written commitment); removes the guilt from continued searching
reframing_moves.example_language: When they file the petition, you can stop applying. Until then, you're still a candidate everywhere
reframing_moves._source: opt_h1b_job_search_real_experiences.txt

reframing_moves.original_framing: 'Big companies are the goal; small companies are a fallback I'd rather avoid'
reframing_moves.reframe: Answer [2] reframes small companies as a different game with different advantages — better skill development, more responsibility, and a proven on-ramp to large companies with experience
reframing_moves.why_it_works: Reframes the hierarchy from a prestige ranking into a strategic choice with genuine tradeoffs; removes the stigma of small companies and converts them from consolation prizes into legitimate starting positions
reframing_moves.example_language: 在美国，有工作经验就是爸爸 (In America, having work experience makes you the boss — experience trumps school prestige)
reframing_moves._source: zhihu_CS专业留学生毕业之后留美的难度有多大.txt

reframing_moves.original_framing: Taking fast food or warehouse jobs is giving up — it has nothing to do with my career
reframing_moves.reframe: Any Canadian work experience is dual-purpose: it generates income and creates real interview stories, Canadian employer references, and English practice that directly improve your professional job search
reframing_moves.why_it_works: It dissolves the psychological separation between 'survival jobs' and 'real career moves' by revealing that the strategic value of the low-status job is invisible from the outside but very real in the hiring process
reframing_moves.example_language: 'These jobs give you real stories to tell in interviews. Every time I answered questions about my fast food work in a professional interview, I felt my English improve noticeably.'
reframing_moves._source: zhihu_加拿大留学生在本地找工作有多难.txt

reframing_moves.original_framing: Other international students in non-CS fields have found jobs in the US, so it must be possible for me too
reframing_moves.reframe: The people you see online are survivors — the majority who didn't find work returned home and are invisible in these forums. You're seeing the 10% success cases and inferring a 50% success rate. CS students complain online because they stayed; other fields are quiet because those students left.
reframing_moves.why_it_works: Directly names and corrects survivorship bias; reframes the 'evidence' the student is using as systematically misleading; encourages more realistic prior about field-specific difficulty
reframing_moves.example_language: '幸存者偏差，其他专业都直接回国了，说话的声音都没有。'
reframing_moves._source: zhihu_在美国名校毕业后找工作有多难.txt

reframing_moves.original_framing: I should wait until I'm sure I want to stay in the US before applying for OPT
reframing_moves.reframe: Applying for OPT is not a commitment to stay — it's buying optionality. You can always choose not to use it. But if you don't apply early, you cannot retroactively recover the months of processing time you lost.
reframing_moves.why_it_works: Reframes OPT application as a low-cost insurance decision rather than a high-stakes life commitment, which removes the psychological barrier of premature certainty
reframing_moves.example_language: 最好是毕业前90天开始申请… 我拖到四月底才决定申请OPT… 因此，我在五月底有幸拿到一份实习offer时，因为没有OPT而完美错过了这份Summer Intern
reframing_moves._source: zhihu_留学生在美国找工作怎么找.txt

reframing_moves.original_framing: I've been rejected everywhere — I must not be good enough to get a job here
reframing_moves.reframe: You are not being evaluated on your ability — you are being filtered by structural barriers (no local experience, thin networks, ATS) that are not measures of quality; the question is not 'am I good enough' but 'which barriers am I hitting and how do I route around them'
reframing_moves.why_it_works: It externalizes the cause of rejection from personal inadequacy to structural obstacles, which are addressable; this prevents premature abandonment and redirects energy toward solvable problems
reframing_moves.example_language: 'Entry-level positions have 100–300 applicants. That's not a test of your ability — that's a logistics problem. You need a different channel, not a better version of yourself.'
reframing_moves._source: zhihu_加拿大留学生在本地找工作有多难.txt
